texts.num.10.9: And if ye go to war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, then ye shall blow an alarm with the trumpets; and ye shall be remembered before the LORD your God, and ye shall be saved from your enemies.
texts.num.10.10: Also in the day of your gladness, and in your solemn days, and in the beginnings of your months, ye shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt-offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace-offerings; that they may be to you for a memorial before your God: I am the LORD your God.
texts.num.10.11: And it came to pass on the twentieth day of the second month, in the second year, that the cloud was taken up from off the tabernacle of the testimony.
texts.num.10.12: And the children of Israel took their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran.
texts.num.10.13: And they first took their journey according to the commandment of the LORD by the hand of Moses.
texts.num.10.14: In the first place went the standard of the camp of the children of Judah according to their armies: and over his host was Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
texts.num.10.15: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Issachar was Nethaneel the son of Zuar.
texts.num.10.16: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Zebulun was Eliab the son of Helon.
texts.num.10.17: And the tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari moved forward, bearing the tabernacle.
texts.num.10.18: And the standard of the camp of Reuben moved forward according to their armies: and over his host was Elizur the son of Shedeur.
texts.num.10.19: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Simeon was Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
texts.num.10.20: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Gad was Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
texts.num.10.21: And the Kohathites moved forward, bearing the sanctuary: and the other set up the tabernacle against they came.
texts.num.10.22: And the standard of the camp of the children of Ephraim moved forward according to their armies: and over his host was Elishama the son of Ammihud.
texts.num.10.23: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Manasseh was Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
texts.num.10.24: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Benjamin was Abidan the son of Gideoni.
texts.num.10.25: And the standard of the camp of the children of Dan moved forward, which was the rear-ward of all the camps throughout their hosts: and over his host was Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
texts.num.10.26: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Asher was Pagiel the son of Ocran.
texts.num.10.27: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Naphtali was Ahira the son of Enan.
texts.num.10.28: Thus were the journeyings of the children of Israel according to their armies, when they moved forward.
texts.num.10.29: And Moses said to Hobab, the son of Raguel the Midianite, Moses's father-in-law, We are journeying to the place of which the LORD said, I will give it to you: come thou with us, and we will do thee good: for the LORD hath spoken good concerning Israel.
texts.num.10.30: And he said to him, I will not go; but I will depart to my own land, and to my kindred.
texts.num.10.31: And he said, Leave us not, I pray thee; forasmuch as thou knowest how we are to encamp in the wilderness, and thou mayest be to us instead of eyes.
texts.num.10.32: And it shall be, if thou wilt go with us, yea, it shall be, that what goodness the LORD shall do to us, the same will we do to thee.
texts.num.10.33: And they departed from the mount of the LORD three days' journey: and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them in the three days' journey, to seek a resting-place for them.
texts.num.10.34: And the cloud of the LORD was upon them by day, when they went out of the camp.
texts.num.10.35: And it came to pass, when the ark moved forward, that Moses said, Arise, LORD, and let thy enemies be scattered; and let them that hate thee flee before thee.
texts.num.10.36: And when it rested, he said, Return, O LORD, to the many thousands of Israel.
texts.num.11.1: And when the people complained, it displeased the LORD; and the LORD heard it: and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the LORD burnt among them, and consumed them that were in the uttermost parts of the camp.
texts.num.11.2: And the people cried to Moses; and when Moses prayed to the LORD, the fire was quenched.
texts.num.11.3: And he called the name of the place Taberah; because the fire of the LORD burnt among them.
texts.num.11.4: And the mixed multitude that was among them fell to lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat?
texts.num.11.5: We remember the fish which we ate in Egypt freely: the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic:
texts.num.11.6: But now our soul is dried away; there is nothing at all, besides this manna, before our eyes.
texts.num.11.7: And the manna was as coriander-seed, and the color of it as the color of bdellium.
texts.num.11.8: And the people went about, and gathered it and ground it in mills, or beat it in a mortar, and baked it in pans, and made cakes of it: and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil.
texts.num.11.9: And when the dew fell upon the camp in the night, the manna fell upon it.
texts.num.11.10: Then Moses heard the people weeping throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent: and the anger of the LORD was kindled greatly: Moses also was displeased.
texts.num.11.11: And Moses said to the LORD, Why hast thou afflicted thy servant? and why have I not found favor in thy sight, that thou layest the burden of all this people upon me?
texts.num.11.12: Have I conceived all this people? have I begotten them, that thou shouldest say to me, Carry them in thy bosom, as a nursing-father beareth the sucking child, to the land which thou sworest to their fathers?
texts.num.11.13: Whence should I have flesh to give to all this people? for they weep to me, saying, Give us flesh, that we may eat.
texts.num.11.14: I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.
texts.num.11.15: And if thou dealest thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favor in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness.
texts.num.11.16: And the LORD said to Moses, Gather to me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom thou knowest to be the elders of the people, and officers over them; and bring them to the tabernacle of the congregation, that they may stand there with thee.
texts.num.11.17: And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou mayest not bear it thyself alone.
texts.num.11.18: And say thou to the people, Sanctify yourselves against to-morrow, and ye shall eat flesh; for ye have wept in the ears of the LORD, saying, Who shall give us flesh to eat? for it was well with us in Egypt: therefore the LORD will give you flesh, and ye shall eat.
texts.num.11.19: Ye shall not eat one day, nor two days, nor five days, neither ten days, nor twenty days;
texts.num.11.20: But even a whole month, until it shall come out at your nostrils, and it be lothsome to you; because ye have despised the LORD who is among you, and have wept before him, saying, Why came we forth out of Egypt?
texts.num.11.21: And Moses said, The people among whom I am, are six hundred thousand footmen; and thou hast said, I will give them flesh, that they may eat a whole month.
texts.num.11.22: Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, to suffice for them? or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered for them, to suffice for them?
texts.num.11.23: And the LORD said to Moses, Is the LORD'S hand shortened? thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass to thee, or not.
texts.num.11.24: And Moses went out, and told the people the words of the LORD, and gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them around the tabernacle.
texts.num.11.25: And the LORD came down in a cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave it to the seventy elders: and it came to pass, that when the spirit rested upon them; they prophesied, and did not cease.
texts.num.11.26: But there remained two of the men in the camp, the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the spirit rested upon them, and they were of them that were described, but went not out to the tabernacle: and they prophesied in the camp.
texts.num.11.27: And there ran a young man, and told Moses, and said, Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.
texts.num.11.28: And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his young men, answered and said, My lord, Moses, forbid them.
texts.num.11.29: And Moses said to him, Enviest thou for my sake? I would that all the LORD'S people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit upon them.
texts.num.11.30: And Moses withdrew into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.
texts.num.11.31: And there went forth a wind from the LORD, and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, as it were a day's journey on this side, and as it were a day's journey on the other side, around the camp, and as it were two cubits high upon the face of the earth.
texts.num.11.32: And the people stood up all that day, and all that night, and all the next day, and they gathered the quails: he that gathered least gathered ten homers: and they spread them all abroad for themselves around the camp.
texts.num.11.33: And while the flesh was yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the LORD was kindled against the people, and the LORD smote the people with a very great plague.
texts.num.11.34: And he called the name of that place Kibroth-hattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted.
texts.num.11.35: And the people journeyed from Kibroth-hattaavah to Hazeroth: and abode at Hazeroth.
texts.num.12.1: And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman whom he had married: for he had married a Cushite woman.
texts.num.12.2: And they said, Hath the LORD indeed spoke only by Moses? hath he not spoke also by us? And the LORD heard it.
texts.num.12.3: (Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men who were upon the face of the earth.)
texts.num.12.4: And the LORD spoke suddenly to Moses, and to Aaron, and to Miriam, Come out ye three to the tabernacle of the congregation. And they three came out.
texts.num.12.5: And the LORD came down in the pillar of the cloud, and stood in the door of the tabernacle, and called Aaron and Miriam: and they both came forth.
texts.num.12.6: And he said, Hear now my words: If there is a prophet among you, I the LORD will make myself known to him in a vision, and will speak to him in a dream.
texts.num.12.7: My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all my house.
texts.num.12.8: With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the LORD shall he behold: why then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
texts.num.12.9: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against them; and he departed.
texts.num.12.10: And the cloud departed from off the tabernacle; and behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and behold, she was leprous.
texts.num.12.11: And Aaron said to Moses, Alas, my lord, I beseech thee, lay not the sin upon us, in which we have done foolishly, and in which we have sinned.
texts.num.12.12: Let her not be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed at the time of his birth.
texts.num.12.13: And Moses cried to the LORD, saying, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee.
texts.num.12.14: And the LORD said to Moses, If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received again.
texts.num.12.15: And Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days: and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again.
texts.num.12.16: And afterward the people removed from Hazeroth, and encamped in the wilderness of Paran.
texts.num.13.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.13.2: Send thou men, that they may search the land of Canaan, which I give to the children of Israel: of every tribe of their fathers shall ye send a man, every one a ruler among them.
texts.num.13.3: And Moses, by the commandment of the LORD, sent them from the wilderness of Paran: all those men were heads of the children of Israel.
texts.num.13.4: And these were their names: Of the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the son of Zaccur.
texts.num.13.5: Of the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori.
texts.num.13.6: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
texts.num.13.7: Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph.
texts.num.13.8: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun.
texts.num.13.9: Of the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu.
texts.num.13.10: Of the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi.
texts.num.13.11: Of the tribe of Joseph, namely, of the tribe of Manassah, Gaddi the son of Susi.
texts.num.13.12: Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli.
texts.num.13.13: Of the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael.
texts.num.13.14: Of the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi.
texts.num.13.15: Of the tribe of Gad, Geuel the son of Machi.
texts.num.13.16: These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to explore the land. And Moses called Oshea the son of Nun Jehoshua.
texts.num.13.17: And Moses sent them to explore the land of Canaan, and said to them, Go ye up this way southward, and ascend the mountain:
texts.num.13.18: And see the land, what it is; and the people that dwell therein, whether they are strong or weak, few or many;
texts.num.13.19: And what the land is that they dwell in, whether it is good or bad; and what cities they are that they dwell in, whether in tents, or in strong holds;
texts.num.13.20: And what the land is, whether it is fertile or barren, whether there is wood in it, or not. And be ye of good courage, and bring of the fruit of the land. Now the time was the time of the first ripe grapes.
texts.num.13.21: So they went up, and searched the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, as men come to Hamath.
texts.num.13.22: And they ascended by the south, and came to Hebron; where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of Anak, were. (Now Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
texts.num.13.23: And they came to the brook of Eshcol, and cut down from thence a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bore it between two upon a staff; and they brought of the pomegranates, and of the figs.
texts.num.13.24: The place was called the brook Eshcol, because of the cluster of grapes which the children of Israel cut down from thence.
texts.num.13.25: And they returned from exploring the land after forty days.
texts.num.13.26: And they went and came to Moses, and to Aaron, and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, to the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and brought back word to them, and to all the congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
texts.num.13.27: And they told him, and said, We came to the land whither thou sentest us, and surely it floweth with milk and honey; and this is the fruit of it.
texts.num.13.28: Nevertheless, the people are strong that dwell in the land, and the cities are walled, and very great: and moreover, we saw the children of Anak there.
texts.num.13.29: The Amalekites dwell in the land of the south: and the Hittites, and the Jebusites, and the Amorites, dwell in the mountains: and the Canaanites dwell by the sea, and by the coast of Jordan.
texts.num.13.30: And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.
texts.num.13.31: But the men that went up with him said, We are not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.
texts.num.13.32: And they brought an evil report of the land which they had searched to the children of Israel, saying, The land through which we have passed to search it, is a land that eateth up its inhabitants; and all the people that we saw in it, are men of a great stature.
texts.num.13.33: And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, who come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.
texts.num.14.1: And all the congregation lifted up their voice, and cried; and the people wept that night.
texts.num.14.2: And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron: and the whole congregation said to them, O that we had died in the land of Egypt! or O that we had died in this wilderness!
texts.num.14.3: And why hath the LORD brought us to this land, to fall by the sword, that our wives and our children should be a prey? were it not better for us to return into Egypt?
texts.num.14.4: And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.
texts.num.14.5: Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Israel.
texts.num.14.6: And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who were of them that searched the land, rent their clothes:
texts.num.14.7: And they spoke to all the company of the children of Israel, saying, The land, which we passed through to search it, is an exceeding good land.
texts.num.14.8: If the LORD delighteth in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it to us; a land which floweth with milk and honey.
texts.num.14.9: Only rebel not ye against the LORD, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defense has departed from them, and the LORD is with us: fear them not.
texts.num.14.10: But all the congregation required to stone them with stones: and the glory of the LORD appeared in the tabernacle of the congregation before all the children of Israel.
texts.num.14.11: And the LORD said to Moses, How long will this people provoke me? and how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have shown among them?
texts.num.14.12: I will smite them with the pestilence, and disinherit them, and will make of thee a greater nation and mightier than they.
texts.num.14.13: And Moses said to the LORD, Then the Egyptians will hear it, (for thou broughtest up this people in thy might from among them;)
texts.num.14.14: And they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land: for they have heard that thou LORD art among this people, that thou LORD art seen face to face, and that thy cloud standeth over them, and that thou goest before them, by day-time in a pillar of a cloud, and in a pillar of fire by night.
texts.num.14.15: Now if thou shalt kill all this people as one man, then the nations which have heard the fame of thee will speak, saying,
texts.num.14.16: Because the LORD was not able to bring this people into the land which he swore to them, therefore he hath slain them in the wilderness.
texts.num.14.17: And now, I beseech thee, let the power of my Lord be great, according as thou hast spoken, saying,
texts.num.14.18: The LORD is long-suffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression, and by no means clearing the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation.
texts.num.14.19: Pardon, I beseech thee, the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of thy mercy, and as thou hast forgiven this people, from Egypt, even until now.
texts.num.14.20: And the LORD said, I have pardoned according to thy word:
texts.num.14.21: But as truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD.
texts.num.14.22: Because all those men who have seen my glory, and my miracles, which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice;
texts.num.14.23: Surely they shall not see the land which I swore to their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it:
texts.num.14.24: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land into which he went; and his seed shall possess it.
texts.num.14.25: (Now the Amalekites, and the Canaanites dwelt in the valley.) To-morrow turn you, and pass into the wilderness, by the way of the Red sea.
texts.num.14.26: And the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
texts.num.14.27: How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against me.
texts.num.14.28: Say to them, As truly as I live, saith the LORD, as ye have spoken in my ears, so will I do to you:
texts.num.14.29: Your carcasses shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, who have murmured against me,
texts.num.14.30: Doubtless ye shall not come into the land concerning which I swore to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.
texts.num.14.31: But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.
texts.num.14.32: But as for you, your carcasses, they shall fall in this wilderness.
texts.num.14.33: And your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years, and bear your lewd deeds, until your carcasses shall be wasted in the wilderness.
texts.num.14.34: After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days (each day for a year) shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years, and ye shall know my breach of promise.
texts.num.14.35: I the LORD have said, I will surely do it to all this evil congregation, that are gathered against me: in this wilderness, they shall be consumed, and there they shall die.
texts.num.14.36: And the men whom Moses sent to search the land, who returned, and made all the congregation to murmur against him, by bringing a slander upon the land,
texts.num.14.37: Even those men that brought the evil report upon the land, died by the plague before the LORD.
texts.num.14.38: But Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who were of the men that went to search the land, lived still.
texts.num.14.39: And Moses told these sayings to all the children of Israel: and the people mourned greatly.
texts.num.14.40: And they rose early in the morning, and ascended to the top of the mountain, saying, Lo, we are here, and will go up to the place which the LORD hath promised: for we have sinned.
texts.num.14.41: And Moses said, Why now do ye transgress the commandment of the LORD? but it shall not prosper.
texts.num.14.42: Go not up, for the LORD is not among you; that ye be not smitten before your enemies.
texts.num.14.43: For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and ye shall fall by the sword: because ye are turned away from the LORD, therefore the LORD will not be with you.
texts.num.14.44: But they presumed to go up to the hill-top: nevertheless the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and Moses, departed not out of the camp.
texts.num.14.45: Then the Amalekites came down, and the Canaanites which dwelt in that hill, and smote them, and discomfited them, even to Hormah.
texts.num.15.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.15.2: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them, When ye shall have come into the land of your habitations, which I give to you,
texts.num.15.3: And will make an offering by fire to the LORD, a burnt-offering, or a sacrifice in performing a vow, or in a free-will-offering, or in your solemn feasts, to make a sweet savor to the LORD, of the herd, or of the flock:
texts.num.15.4: Then shall he that offereth his offering to the LORD bring a meat-offering of a tenth part of flour mingled with the fourth part of a hin of oil.
texts.num.15.5: And the fourth part of a hin of wine for a drink-offering shalt thou prepare with the burnt-offering or sacrifice, for one lamb.
texts.num.15.6: Or for a ram, thou shalt prepare for a meat-offering two tenth parts of flour mingled with the third part of a hin of oil.
texts.num.15.7: And for a drink-offering thou shalt offer the third part of a hin of wine, for a sweet savor to the LORD.
texts.num.15.8: And when thou preparest a bullock for a burnt-offering, or for a sacrifice in performing a vow, or peace-offerings to the LORD:
texts.num.15.9: Then shall he bring with a bullock a meat-offering of three tenth parts of flour mingled with half a hin of oil.
texts.num.15.10: And thou shalt bring for a drink-offering half a hin of wine, for an offering made by fire, of a sweet savor to the LORD:
texts.num.15.11: Thus shall it be done for one bullock, or for one ram, or for a lamb, or a kid.
texts.num.15.12: According to the number that ye shall prepare, so shall ye do to every one according to their number.
texts.num.15.13: All that are born in the country shall do these things after this manner, in offering an offering made by fire, of a sweet savor to the LORD.
texts.num.15.14: And if a stranger shall sojourn with you, or whoever shall be among you in your generations, and will offer an offering made by fire, of a sweet savor to the LORD; as ye do, so he shall do.
texts.num.15.15: One ordinance shall be both for you of the congregation, and also for the stranger that sojourneth with you, an ordinance for ever in your generations: as ye are, so shall the stranger be before the LORD.
texts.num.15.16: One law and one manner shall be for you, and for the stranger that sojourneth with you.
texts.num.15.17: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.15.18: Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them, When ye come into the land whither I bring you,
texts.num.15.19: Then it shall be, that when ye eat of the bread of the land, ye shall offer up a heave-offering to the LORD.
texts.num.15.20: Ye shall offer a cake of the first of your dough for a heave-offering: as ye do the heave-offering of the threshing-floor, so shall ye heave it.
texts.num.15.21: Of the first of your dough ye shall give to the LORD a heave-offering in your generations.
texts.num.15.22: And if ye have erred, and not observed all these commandments which the LORD hath spoken to Moses,
texts.num.15.23: Even all that the LORD hath commanded you by the hand of Moses, from the day that the LORD commanded Moses, and henceforward among your generations;
texts.num.15.24: Then it shall be, if aught shall be committed by ignorance without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall offer one young bullock for a burnt-offering, for a sweet savor to the LORD, with his meat-offering, and his drink-offering, according to the manner, and one kid of the goats for a sin-offering.
texts.num.15.25: And the priest shall make an atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and it shall be forgiven them; for it is ignorance: and they shall bring their offering, a sacrifice made by fire to the LORD, and their sin-offering before the LORD, for their ignorance:
texts.num.15.26: And it shall be forgiven all the congregation of the children of Israel, and the stranger that sojourneth among them; seeing all the people were in ignorance.
texts.num.15.27: And if any soul shall sin through ignorance, then he shall bring a she-goat of the first year for a sin-offering.
texts.num.15.28: And the priest shall make an atonement for the soul that sinneth ignorantly, when he sinneth by ignorance before the LORD, to make an atonement for him; and it shall be forgiven him.
texts.num.15.29: Ye shall have one law for him that sinneth through ignorance, both for him that is born among the children of Israel, and for the stranger that sojourneth among them.
texts.num.15.30: But the soul that doeth aught presumptuously, whether he be born in the land, or a stranger, the same reproacheth the LORD; and that soul shall be cut off from among his people.
texts.num.15.31: Because he hath despised the word of the LORD, and hath broken his commandment, that soul shall utterly be cut off; his iniquity shall be upon him.
texts.num.15.32: And while the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man that gathered sticks upon the sabbath-day.
texts.num.15.33: And they that found him gathering sticks brought him to Moses and Aaron, and to all the congregation.
texts.num.15.34: And they put him in custody, because it was not declared what should be done to him.
texts.num.15.35: And the LORD said to Moses, The man shall surely be put to death: all the congregation shall stone him with stones without the camp.
texts.num.15.36: And all the congregation brought him without the camp, and stoned him with stones, and he died; as the LORD commanded Moses.
texts.num.15.37: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.15.38: Speak to the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes on the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a ribin of blue:
texts.num.15.39: And it shall be to you for a fringe, that ye may look upon it, and remember all the commandments of the LORD, and do them; and that ye seek not after your own heart and your own eyes, after which ye use to go astray:
texts.num.15.40: That ye may remember, and do all my commandments, and be holy to your God.
texts.num.15.41: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am the LORD your God.
texts.num.16.1: Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, took men:
texts.num.16.2: And they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel, two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown:
texts.num.16.3: And they assembled themselves against Moses and against Aaron, and said to them, Ye take too much upon you, seeing all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them: why then do ye raise yourselves above the congregation of the LORD?
texts.num.16.4: And when Moses heard it, he fell upon his face:
texts.num.16.5: And he spoke to Korah and to all his company, saying, Even to-morrow the LORD will show who are his, and who is holy; and will cause him to come near to him: even him whom he hath chosen will he cause to come near to him.
texts.num.16.6: This do; Take you censers, Korah, and all his company;
texts.num.16.7: And put fire in them, and put incense in them before the LORD to-morrow: and it shall be that the man whom the LORD doth choose, he shall be holy: ye take too much upon you, ye sons of Levi.
texts.num.16.8: And Moses said to Korah, Hear, I pray you, ye sons of Levi:
texts.num.16.9: Seemeth it but a small thing to you, that the God of Israel hath separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to himself to do the service of the tabernacle of the LORD, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
texts.num.16.10: And he hath brought thee near to him, and all thy brethren the sons of Levi with thee: and seek ye the priesthood also?
texts.num.16.11: For which cause both thou and all thy company are assembled against the LORD: and what is Aaron, that ye murmur against him?
texts.num.16.12: And Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab: who said, We will not come up:
texts.num.16.13: Is it a small thing that thou hast brought us out of a land that floweth with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, except thou make thyself altogether a prince over us?
texts.num.16.14: Moreover, thou hast not brought us into a land that floweth with milk and honey, or given us inheritance of fields and vineyards: wilt thou put out the eyes of these men? we will not come up.
texts.num.16.15: And Moses was very wroth, and said to the LORD, Respect not thou their offering: I have not taken one ass from them, neither have I hurt one of them.
texts.num.16.16: And Moses said to Korah, Be thou and all thy company before the LORD, thou, and they, and Aaron, to-morrow:
texts.num.16.17: And take every man his censer, and put incense in them, and bring ye before the LORD every man his censer, two hundred and fifty censers; thou also and Aaron each of you his censer.
texts.num.16.18: And they took every man his censer, and put fire in them, and laid incense on them, and stood in the door of the tabernacle of the congregation with Moses and Aaron.
texts.num.16.19: And Korah gathered all the congregation against them to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the congregation.
texts.num.16.20: And the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
texts.num.16.21: Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment.
texts.num.16.22: And they fell upon their faces, and said, O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and wilt thou be wroth with all the congregation?
texts.num.16.23: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.16.24: Speak to the congregation, saying, Withdraw yourselves from about the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.
texts.num.16.25: And Moses rose up, and went to Dathan and Abiram; and the elders of Israel followed him.
texts.num.16.26: And he spoke to the congregation, saying, Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest ye be consumed in all their sins.
texts.num.16.27: So they withdrew from the tabernacle of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, on every side: and Dathan and Abiram came out, and stood in the door of their tents, and their wives, and their sons, and their little children.
texts.num.16.28: And Moses said, by this ye shall know that the LORD hath sent me to do all these works: for I have not done them of my own mind.
texts.num.16.29: If these men shall die the common death of all men, or if they be visited after the visitation of all men; then the LORD hath not sent me.
texts.num.16.30: But if the LORD shall make a new thing, and the earth shall open her mouth, and swallow them up, with all that appertain to them, and they go down quick into the pit; then ye shall understand that these men have provoked the LORD.
texts.num.16.31: And it came to pass, as he had made an end of speaking all these words, that the ground cleaved asunder that was under them:
texts.num.16.32: And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained to Korah, and all their goods.
texts.num.16.33: They, and all that appertained to them went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation.
texts.num.16.34: And all Israel that were round about them, fled at the cry of them: for they said, Lest the earth swallow us up also.
texts.num.16.35: And there came out a fire from the LORD, and consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.
texts.num.16.36: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.16.37: Speak to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, that he take up the censers out of the burning, and scatter thou the fire yonder; for they are hallowed.
texts.num.16.38: The censers of these sinners against their own souls, let them make them broad plates for a covering of the altar: for they offered them before the LORD, therefore they are hallowed: and they shall be a sign to the children of Israel.
texts.num.16.39: And Eleazar the priest took the brazen censers, with which they that were burnt had offered; and they were made broad plates for a covering of the altar:
texts.num.16.40: To be a memorial to the children of Israel, that no stranger, who is not of the seed of Aaron, should come near to offer incense before the LORD; that he may not be as Korah, and as his company: as the LORD said to him by the hand of Moses.
texts.num.16.41: But on the morrow all the congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron, saying, Ye have killed the people of the LORD.
texts.num.16.42: And it came to pass when the congregation was gathered against Moses and against Aaron, that they looked towards the tabernacle of the congregation: and behold, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
texts.num.16.43: And Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle of the congregation.
texts.num.16.44: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.16.45: Remove from among this congregation, that I may consume them as in a moment. And they fell upon their faces.
texts.num.16.46: And Moses said to Aaron, Take a censer, and put fire in it from off the altar, and put on incense, and go quickly to the congregation, and make an atonement for them: for there is wrath gone out from the LORD; the plague is begun.
texts.num.16.47: And Aaron took as Moses commanded, and ran into the midst of the congregation; and behold, the plague was begun among the people: and he put on incense, and made an atonement for the people.
texts.num.16.48: And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.
texts.num.16.49: Now they that died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, besides them that died about the matter of Korah.
texts.num.16.50: And Aaron returned to Moses at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation: and the plague was stayed.
texts.num.17.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.17.2: Speak to the children of Israel, and take of every one of them a rod according to the house of their fathers, of all their princes according to the house of their fathers, twelve rods: write thou every man's name upon his rod.
texts.num.17.3: And thou shalt write Aaron's name upon the rod of Levi: for one rod shall be for the head of the house of their fathers.
texts.num.17.4: And thou shalt lay them in the tabernacle of the congregation before the testimony, where I will meet with you.
texts.num.17.5: And it shall come to pass, that the man's rod, whom I shall choose, shall blossom: and I will make to cease from me the murmurings of the children of Israel, by which they murmur against you.
texts.num.17.6: And Moses spoke to the children of Israel, and every one of their princes gave him a rod apiece, for each prince one, according to their fathers' houses, even twelve rods: and the rod of Aaron was among their rods.
texts.num.17.7: And Moses laid the rods before the LORD in the tabernacle of witness.
texts.num.17.8: And it came to pass, that on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi had budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds.
texts.num.17.9: And Moses brought out all the rods from before the LORD to all the children of Israel: and they looked, and took every man his rod.
texts.num.17.10: And the LORD said to Moses, Bring Aaron's rod again, before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the rebels; and thou shalt quite take away their murmurings from me, that they die not.
texts.num.17.11: And Moses did so: as the LORD commanded him, so did he.
texts.num.17.12: And the children of Israel spoke to Moses, saying, Behold, we die, we perish, we all perish.
texts.num.17.13: Whoever approacheth the tabernacle of the LORD shall die: shall we be consumed with dying?
texts.num.18.1: And the LORD said to Aaron, Thou and thy sons and thy father's house with thee shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary: and thou and thy sons with thee shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood.
texts.num.18.2: And thy brethren also of the tribe of Levi, the tribe of thy father, bring thou with thee, that they may be joined to thee, and minister to thee: but thou and thy sons with thee shall minister before the tabernacle of witness.
texts.num.18.3: And they shall keep thy charge, and the charge of all the tabernacle: only they shall not come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, that neither they, nor ye also, die.
texts.num.18.4: And they shall be joined to thee, and keep the charge of the tabernacle of the congregation, for all the service of the tabernacle: and a stranger shall not come nigh to you.
texts.num.18.5: And ye shall keep the charge of the sanctuary, and the charge of the altar: that there be no wrath any more upon the children of Israel.
texts.num.18.6: And I, behold, I have taken your brethren the Levites from among the children of Israel: to you they are given as a gift for the LORD, to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.
texts.num.18.7: Therefore thou and thy sons with thee shall keep your priest's office for every thing of the altar, and within the vail; and ye shall serve: I have given your priest's office to you as a service of gift: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.
texts.num.18.8: And the LORD spoke to Aaron, Behold, I also have given thee the charge of my heave-offerings of all the hallowed things of the children of Israel; to thee have I given them by reason of the anointing, and to thy sons, by an ordinance for ever.
texts.num.18.9: This shall be thine of the most holy things reserved from the fire: every oblation of theirs, every meat-offering of theirs, and every sin-offering of theirs, and every trespass-offering of theirs, which they shall render to me, shall be most holy for thee and for thy sons.
texts.num.18.10: In the most holy place shalt thou eat it; every male shall eat it: it shall be holy to thee.
texts.num.18.11: And this is thine; the heave-offering of their gift, with all the wave-offerings of the children of Israel: I have given them to thee, and to thy sons, and to thy daughters with thee, by a statute for ever: every one that is clean in thy house shall eat of it.
texts.num.18.12: All the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and of the wheat, the first-fruits of them which they shall offer to the LORD, them have I given to thee.
texts.num.18.13: And whatever is first ripe in the land, which they shall bring to the LORD, shall be thine; every one that is clean in thy house shall eat of it.
texts.num.18.14: Every thing devoted in Israel shall be thine.
texts.num.18.15: Every thing that openeth the matrix in all flesh, which they bring to the LORD, whether of men or beast, shall be thine: nevertheless, the first born of man shalt thou surely redeem, and the firstling of unclean beasts shalt thou redeem.
texts.num.18.16: And those that are to be redeemed from a month old shalt thou redeem, according to thy estimation, for the money of five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs.
texts.num.18.17: But the firstling of a cow, or the firstling of a sheep, or the firstling of a goat, thou shalt not redeem; they are holy: thou shalt sprinkle their blood upon the altar, and shalt burn their fat for an offering made by fire, for a sweet savor to the LORD.
texts.num.18.18: And the flesh of them shall be thine, as the wave-breast and as the right shoulder are thine
texts.num.18.19: All the heave-offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer to the LORD, have I given to thee, and to thy sons and thy daughters with thee, by a statute for ever: it is a covenant of salt for ever before the LORD to thee and to thy seed with thee.
texts.num.18.20: And the LORD spoke to Aaron, Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither shalt thou have any part among them: I am thy part and thy inheritance among the children of Israel.
texts.num.18.21: And behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, even the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.
texts.num.18.22: Neither must the children of Israel henceforth come nigh the tabernacle of the congregation, lest they bear sin, and die.
texts.num.18.23: But the Levites shall do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, and they shall bear their iniquity: It shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations, that among the children of Israel they have no inheritance.
texts.num.18.24: But the tithes of the children of Israel, which they offer as a heave-offering to the LORD, I have given to the Levites to inherit: therefore I have said to them, Among the children of Israel they shall have no inheritance.
texts.num.18.25: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.18.26: Thus speak to the Levites, and say to them, When ye take of the children of Israel the tithes which I have given you from them for your inheritance, then ye shall offer up a heave-offering of it for the LORD, even a tenth part of the tithe.
texts.num.18.27: And this your heave-offering shall be reckoned to you, as though it were the corn of the threshing-floor, and as the fullness of the wine-press.
texts.num.18.28: Thus ye also shall offer a heave-offering to the LORD of all your tithes which ye receive of the children of Israel; and ye shall give of them the LORD'S heave-offering to Aaron the priest.
texts.num.18.29: Out of all your gifts ye shall offer every heave-offering of the LORD, of all the best of it, even its hallowed part out of it.
texts.num.18.30: Therefore thou shalt say to them, When ye have heaved from it the best of it, then it shall be counted to the Levites as the increase of the threshing-floor, and as the increase of the wine-press.
texts.num.18.31: And ye shall eat it in every place, ye and your households: for it is your reward for your service in the tabernacle of the congregation.
texts.num.18.32: And ye shall bear no sin by reason of it, when ye have heaved from it the best of it: neither shall ye pollute the holy things of the children of Israel, lest ye die.
texts.num.19.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
texts.num.19.2: This is the ordinance of the law which the LORD hath commanded, saying, Speak to the children of Israel, that they bring thee a red heifer without spot, in which is no blemish, and upon which never came a yoke:
texts.num.19.3: And ye shall give her to Eleazar the priest, that he may bring her forth without the camp, and one shall slay her before his face:
texts.num.19.4: And Eleazar the priest shall take of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle of her blood directly before the tabernacle of the congregation seven times:
texts.num.19.5: And one shall burn the heifer in his sight; her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, with her dung, shall he burn:
texts.num.19.6: And the priest shall take cedar-wood, and hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the midst of the burning of the heifer.
texts.num.19.7: Then the priest shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he shall come into the camp, and the priest shall be unclean until the evening.
texts.num.19.8: And he that burneth her shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and shall be unclean until the evening.
texts.num.19.9: And a man that is clean shall gather the ashes of the heifer, and lay them without the camp in a clean place, and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel, for a water of separation: it is a purification for sin.
texts.num.19.10: And he that gathereth the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening: and it shall be to the children of Israel, and to the stranger that sojourneth among them, for a statute for ever.
texts.num.19.11: He that toucheth the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days.
texts.num.19.12: He shall purify himself with it on the third day, and on the seventh day he shall be clean: but if he shall not purify himself the third day, then the seventh day he shall not be clean.
texts.num.19.13: Whoever toucheth the dead body of any man that is dead, and purifieth not himself, defileth the tabernacle of the LORD; and that soul shall be cut off from Israel: because the water of separation was not sprinkled upon him, he shall be unclean; his uncleanness is yet upon him.
texts.num.19.14: This is the law, when a man dieth in a tent: all that come into the tent, and all that is in the tent, shall be unclean seven days.
texts.num.19.15: And every open vessel, which hath no covering bound upon it, is unclean.
texts.num.19.16: And whoever toucheth one that is slain with a sword in the open fields, or a dead body, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.
texts.num.19.17: And for an unclean person they shall take of the ashes of the burnt heifer of purification for sin, and running water shall be put to it in a vessel:
texts.num.19.18: And a clean person shall take hyssop, and dip it in the water, and sprinkle it upon the tent, and upon all the vessels, and upon the persons that were there, and upon him that touched a bone, or one slain, or one dead, or a grave:
texts.num.19.19: And the clean person shall sprinkle upon the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day: and on the seventh day he shall purify himself, and wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and shall be clean at evening.
texts.num.19.20: But the man that shall be unclean, and shall not purify himself, that soul shall be cut off from among the congregation, because he hath defiled the sanctuary of the LORD: the water of separation hath not been sprinkled upon him: he is unclean.
texts.num.19.21: And it shall be a perpetual statute to them, that he that sprinkleth the water of separation shall wash his clothes; and he that toucheth the water of separation shall be unclean until the evening.
texts.num.19.22: And whatever the unclean person toucheth shall be unclean; and the soul that toucheth it shall be unclean until the evening.
texts.num.20.1: Then came the children of Israel, even the whole congregation, into the desert of Zin in the first month; and the people abode in Kadesh; and Miriam died there, and was buried there.
texts.num.20.2: And there was no water for the congregation: and they assembled themselves against Moses and against Aaron.
texts.num.20.3: And the people chid with Moses, and spoke, saying, O that we had died when our brethren died before the LORD!
texts.num.20.4: And why have ye brought the congregation of the LORD into this wilderness, that we and our cattle should die there?
texts.num.20.5: And why have ye conducted us from Egypt, to bring us to this evil place? it is no place of seed, or of figs, or of vines, or of pomegranates; neither is there any water to drink.
texts.num.20.6: And Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and they fell upon their faces: and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
texts.num.20.7: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.20.8: Take the rod, and convene thou the assembly, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye to the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth its water, and thou shalt bring forth to them water out of the rock: so thou shalt give drink to the congregation and their beasts.
texts.num.20.9: And Moses took the rod from before the LORD, as he commanded him.
texts.num.20.10: And Moses and Aaron assembled the congregation before the rock, and he said to them, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?
texts.num.20.11: And Moses lifted his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.
texts.num.20.12: And the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.
texts.num.20.13: This is the water of Meribah; because the children of Israel strove with the LORD, and he was sanctified in them.
texts.num.20.14: And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, Thus saith thy brother Israel, Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us:
texts.num.20.15: How our fathers went down into Egypt, and we have dwelt in Egypt a long time; and the Egyptians afflicted us, and our fathers:
texts.num.20.16: And when we cried to the LORD, he heard our voice, and sent an angel, and hath brought us forth from Egypt: and behold, we are in Kadesh, a city in the uttermost of thy border:
texts.num.20.17: Let us pass, I pray thee, through thy country: we will not pass through the fields, or through the vineyards, neither will we drink of the water of the wells: we will go by the king's high-way, we will not turn to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed thy borders.
texts.num.20.18: And Edom said to him, Thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword.
texts.num.20.19: And the children of Israel said to him, We will go by the highway: and if I and my cattle drink of thy water, then I will pay for it: I will only, without doing any thing else, go through on my feet.
texts.num.20.20: And he said, Thou shalt not go through. And Edom came out against him with many people, and with a strong hand.
texts.num.20.21: Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border: wherefore Israel turned away from him.
texts.num.20.22: And the children of Israel, even the whole congregation, journeyed from Kadesh, and came to mount Hor.
texts.num.20.23: And the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron in mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, saying,
texts.num.20.24: Aaron shall be gathered to his people: for he shall not enter into the land which I have given to the children of Israel, because ye rebelled against my word at the water of Meribah.
texts.num.20.25: Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up to mount Hor:
texts.num.20.26: And strip Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son: and Aaron shall be gathered to his people, and shall die there.
texts.num.20.27: And Moses did as the LORD commanded: and they ascended mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation.
texts.num.20.28: And Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there on the top of the mount: and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mount.
texts.num.20.29: And when all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, they mourned for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.
texts.num.21.1: And when king Arad the Canaanite, who dwelt in the south, heard that Israel came by the way of the spies; then he fought against Israel, and took some of them prisoners.
texts.num.21.2: And Israel vowed a vow to the LORD, and said, If thou wilt indeed deliver this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities.
texts.num.21.3: And the LORD hearkened to the voice of Israel, and delivered up the Canaanites; and they utterly destroyed them and their cities: and he called the name of the place Hormah.
texts.num.21.4: And they journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red sea, to compass the land of Edom: and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way.
texts.num.21.5: And the people spoke against God, and against Moses, Why have ye brought us out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul lotheth this light bread.
texts.num.21.6: And the LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and many people of Israel died.
texts.num.21.7: Therefore the people came to Moses, and said, We have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD, and against thee; pray to the LORD, that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people.
texts.num.21.8: And the LORD said to Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.
texts.num.21.9: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
texts.num.21.10: And the children of Israel moved forward, and pitched in Oboth.
texts.num.21.11: And they journeyed from Oboth, and pitched at Ije-abarim, in the wilderness which is before Moab, towards the sun-rising.
texts.num.21.12: From thence they removed, and pitched in the valley of Zared.
texts.num.21.13: From thence they removed, and pitched on the other side of Arnon, which is in the wilderness that cometh out of the coasts of the Amorites: for Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
texts.num.21.14: Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the LORD, What he did in the Red sea, and in the brooks of Arnon,
texts.num.21.15: And at the stream of the brooks that goeth down to the dwelling of Ar, and lieth upon the border of Moab.
texts.num.21.16: And from thence they went to Beer: that is the well of which the LORD spoke to Moses, Assemble the people, and I will give them water.
texts.num.21.17: Then Israel sung this song, Spring up, O well; sing ye to it:
texts.num.21.18: The princes digged the well, the nobles of the people digged it, by the direction of the lawgiver, with their staffs. And from the wilderness they went to Mattanah:
texts.num.21.19: And from Mattanah to Nahaliel: and from Nahaliel to Bamoth:
texts.num.21.20: And from Bamoth in the valley, that is in the country of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looketh towards Jeshimon.
texts.num.21.21: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
texts.num.21.22: Let me pass through thy land: we will not turn into the fields, or into the vineyards; we will not drink of the waters of the well: but we will go along by the king's high-way, until we have past thy borders.
texts.num.21.23: And Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon collected all his people, and went out against Israel into the wilderness: and he came to Jahaz, and fought against Israel:
texts.num.21.24: And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from Arnon to Jabbok, even to the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.
texts.num.21.25: And Israel took all these cities: and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all its villages.
texts.num.21.26: For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab, and taken all his land out of his hand, even to Arnon.
texts.num.21.27: Wherefore they that speak in proverbs say, Come into Heshbon, let the city of Sihon be built and prepared.
texts.num.21.28: For there has a fire gone out of Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon: it hath consumed Ar of Moab, and the lords of the high places of Arnon.
texts.num.21.29: Woe to thee, Moab! thou art undone, O people of Chemosh: he hath given his sons that escaped, and his daughters, into captivity to Sihon king of the Amorites.
texts.num.21.30: We have shot at them; Heshbon has perished even to Dibon, and we have laid them waste even to Nophah, which reacheth to Medeba.
texts.num.21.31: Thus Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorites.
texts.num.21.32: And Moses sent to explore Jaazer, and they took its villages, and drove out the Amorites that were there.
texts.num.21.33: And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan: and Og the king of Bashan went out against them, he, and all his people, to the battle at Edrei.
texts.num.21.34: And the LORD said to Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand, and all his people, and his land; and thou shalt do to him as thou didst to Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Heshbon.
texts.num.21.35: So they smote him, and his sons, and all his people, until there was none left to him alive: and they possessed his land.
texts.num.22.1: And the children of Israel moved forward, and pitched in the plains of Moab on this side of Jordan by Jericho.
texts.num.22.2: And Balak the son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
texts.num.22.3: And Moab was greatly afraid of the people, because they were many: and Moab was distressed because of the children of Israel.
texts.num.22.4: And Moab said to the elders of Midian, Now shall this company lick up all that are around us, as the ox licketh up the grass of the field. And Balak the son of Zippor was king of the Moabites at that time.
texts.num.22.5: He sent messengers therefore to Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, Behold, there has a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me:
texts.num.22.6: Come now therefore, I pray thee, Curse for me this people; for they are too mighty for me: it may be I shall prevail, that we may smite them, and that I may drive them out of the land: for I know that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.
texts.num.22.7: And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the rewards of divination in their hand; and they came to Balaam, and spoke to him the words of Balak.
texts.num.22.8: And he said to them, Lodge here this night, and I will bring you word again, as the LORD shall speak to me: and the princes of Moab abode with Balaam.
texts.num.22.9: And God came to Balaam, and said, What men are these with thee?
texts.num.22.10: And Balaam said to God, Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, hath sent to me, saying,
texts.num.22.11: Behold, there has a people come out of Egypt, which covereth the face of the earth: come now, curse them for me: it may be I shall be able to overcome them, and drive them out.
texts.num.22.12: And God said to Balaam, Thou shalt not go with them; thou shalt not curse the people: for they are blessed.
texts.num.22.13: And Balaam rose in the morning, and said to the princes of Balak, Depart into your land: for the LORD refuseth to give me leave to go with you.
texts.num.22.14: And the princes of Moab rose up, and they went to Balak, and said, Balaam refuseth to come with us.
texts.num.22.15: And Balak sent yet again princes, more, and more honorable than they.
texts.num.22.16: And they came to Balaam, and said to him, Thus saith Balak the son of Zippor, Let nothing, I pray thee, hinder thee from coming to me:
texts.num.22.17: For I will promote thee to very great honor, and I will do whatever thou sayest to me: come therefore, I pray thee, curse this people for me.
texts.num.22.18: And Balaam answered and said to the servants of Balak, If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the LORD my God, to do less or more.
texts.num.22.19: Now therefore, I pray you, tarry ye also here this night, that I may know what the LORD will say to me more.
texts.num.22.20: And God came to Balaam at night, and said to him, If the men come to call thee, rise and go with them; but yet the word which I shall say to thee, that shalt thou perform.
texts.num.22.21: And Balaam rose in the morning, and saddled his ass, and went with the princes of Moab.
texts.num.22.22: And God's anger was kindled because he went: and the angel of the LORD stood in the way for an adversary against him. Now he was riding upon his ass, and his two servants were with him.
texts.num.22.23: And the ass saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand: and the ass turned aside out of the way, and went into the field: and Balaam smote the ass, to turn her into the way.
texts.num.22.24: But the angel of the LORD stood in a path of the vineyards, a wall being on this side, and a wall on that side.
texts.num.22.25: And when the ass saw the angel of the LORD, she thrust herself against the wall, and crushed Balaam's foot against the wall: and he smote her again.
texts.num.22.26: And the angel of the LORD went further, and stood in a narrow place, where was no way to turn either to the right hand or to the left.
texts.num.22.27: And when the ass saw the angel of the LORD, she fell down under Balaam: and Balaam's anger was kindled, and he smote the ass with a staff.
texts.num.22.28: And the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she said to Balaam, What have I done to thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?
texts.num.22.29: And Balaam said to the ass, Because thou hast mocked me: I would there were a sword in my hand, for now would I kill thee.
texts.num.22.30: And the ass said to Balaam, Am not I thy ass, upon which thou hast rid ever since I was thine to this day? was I ever wont to do so to thee? And he said, Nay.
texts.num.22.31: Then the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand: and he bowed down his head, and fell flat on his face.
texts.num.22.32: And the angel of the LORD said to him, Why hast thou smitten thy ass these three times? behold, I went out to withstand thee, because thy way is perverse before me:
texts.num.22.33: And the ass saw me, and turned from me these three times: unless she had turned from me, surely now also I had slain thee, and saved her alive.
texts.num.22.34: And Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, I have sinned; for I knew not that thou stoodest in the way against me: now therefore, if it displeaseth thee, I will return again.
texts.num.22.35: And the angel of the LORD said to Balaam, Go with the men: but only the word that I shall speak to thee, that thou shalt speak: So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.
texts.num.22.36: And when Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went out to meet him to a city of Moab, which is in the border of Arnon, which is in the utmost limit.
texts.num.22.37: And Balak said to Balaam, Did I not earnestly send to thee to call thee? why camest thou not to me? am I not able indeed to promote thee to honor?
texts.num.22.38: And Balaam said to Balak, Lo, I have come to thee: have I now any power at all to say any thing? the word that God putteth in my mouth, that shall I speak.
texts.num.22.39: And Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kirjath-huzoth.
texts.num.22.40: And Balak offered oxen and sheep, and sent to Balaam, and to the princes that were with him.
texts.num.22.41: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Balak took Balaam, and conducted him to the high places of Baal, that thence he might see the utmost part of the people.
texts.num.23.1: And Balaam said to Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven oxen and seven rams.
texts.num.23.2: And Balak did as Balaam had spoken; and Balak and Balaam offered on every altar a bullock and a ram.
texts.num.23.3: And Balaam said to Balak, Stand by thy burnt-offering, and I will go: it may be the LORD will come to meet me: and whatever he showeth me I will tell thee. And he went to a high place.
texts.num.23.4: And God met Balaam: and he said to him, I have prepared seven altars, and I have offered upon every altar a bullock and a ram.
texts.num.23.5: And the LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth, and said, Return to Balak, and thus thou shalt speak.
texts.num.23.6: And he returned to him and lo, he stood by his burnt-sacrifice, he, and all the princes of Moab.
texts.num.23.7: And he took up his parable, and said, Balak the king of Moab hath brought me from Aram, out of the mountains of the east, saying, Come, curse Jacob for me, and come, defy Israel.
texts.num.23.8: How shall I curse, whom God hath not cursed? or how shall I defy, whom the LORD hath not defied?
texts.num.23.9: For from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I behold him: lo, the people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations.
texts.num.23.10: Who can count the dust of Jacob, and the number of the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my last end be like his!
texts.num.23.11: And Balak said to Balaam, What hast thou done to me? I took thee to curse my enemies, and behold, thou hast blessed them altogether.
texts.num.23.12: And he answered and said, Must I not take heed to speak that which the LORD hath put in my mouth?
texts.num.23.13: And Balak said to him, Come, I pray thee, with me to another place, from whence thou mayest see them: thou shalt see but the utmost part of them, and shalt not see them all: and from thence curse them for me.
texts.num.23.14: And he brought him into the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered a bullock and a ram on every altar.
texts.num.23.15: And he said to Balak, Stand here by thy burnt-offering, while I meet the LORD yonder.
texts.num.23.16: And the LORD met Balaam, and put a word in his mouth, and said, Go again to Balak, and say thus.
texts.num.23.17: And when he came to him, behold, he stood by his burnt-offering, and the princes of Moab with him. And Balak said to him, What hath the LORD spoken?
texts.num.23.18: And he took up his parable, and said, Rise, Balak, and hear; hearken to me, thou son of Zippor:
texts.num.23.19: God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoke, and shall he not make it good?
texts.num.23.20: Behold, I have received commandment to bless: and he hath blessed, and I cannot reverse it.
texts.num.23.21: He hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob, neither hath he seen perverseness in Israel; the LORD his God is with him, and the shout of a king is among them.
texts.num.23.22: God brought them out of Egypt; he hath as it were the strength of a unicorn.
texts.num.23.23: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel: according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God wrought!
texts.num.23.24: Behold, the people shall rise up as a great lion, and lift up himself as a young lion: he shall not lie down until he shall eat of the prey, and drink the blood of the slain.
texts.num.23.25: And Balak said to Balaam, Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all.
texts.num.23.26: But Balaam answered and said to Balak, Did I not tell thee, saying, All that the LORD speaketh, that I must do?
texts.num.23.27: And Balak said to Balaam, Come, I pray thee, I will bring thee to another place; perhaps it will please God that thou mayest from thence curse them for me.
texts.num.23.28: And Balak brought Balaam to the top of Peor, that looketh towards Jeshimon.
texts.num.23.29: And Balaam said to Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullocks and seven rams.
texts.num.23.30: And Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bullock and a ram on every altar.
texts.num.24.1: And when Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he went not, as at other times, to seek for enchantments, but he set his face toward the wilderness.
texts.num.24.2: And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Israel abiding in his tents according to their tribes, and the spirit of God came upon him.
texts.num.24.3: And he took up his parable, and said, Balaam the son of Beor hath said, and the man whose eyes are open hath said:
texts.num.24.4: He hath said, who heard the words of God, who saw the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open:
texts.num.24.5: How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!
texts.num.24.6: As the valleys are they spread forth, as gardens by the river's side, as the trees of lign-aloes which the LORD hath planted, and as cedar-trees beside the waters.
texts.num.24.7: He shall pour the water out of his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters, and his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted.
texts.num.24.8: God brought him forth from Egypt; he hath as it were the strength of a unicorn: he shall eat up the nations his enemies, and shall break their bones, and pierce them through with his arrows.
texts.num.24.9: He couched, he lay down as a lion, and as a great lion: who shall rouse him? Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee.
texts.num.24.10: And Balak's anger was kindled against Balaam, and he smote his hands together: and Balak said to Balaam, I called thee to curse my enemies, and behold, thou hast altogether blessed them these three times.
texts.num.24.11: Therefore now flee thou to thy place: I thought to promote thee to great honor; but lo, the LORD hath kept thee back from honor.
texts.num.24.12: And Balaam said to Balak, Did I not speak also to thy messengers whom thou sentest to me, saying,
texts.num.24.13: If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the commandment of the LORD, to do either good or bad of my own mind; but what the LORD saith, that will I speak?
texts.num.24.14: And now, behold, I go to my people: come therefore, I will advertise thee what this people will do to thy people in the latter days.
texts.num.24.15: And he took up his parable, and said, Balaam the son of Beor hath said, and the man whose eyes are open hath said:
texts.num.24.16: He hath said, who heard the words of God, and knew the knowledge of the Most High, who saw the vision of the Almighty, falling into a trance, but having his eyes open:
texts.num.24.17: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Scepter shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.
texts.num.24.18: And Edom shall be a possession, Seir also shall be a possession for his enemies; and Israel shall do valiantly.
texts.num.24.19: Out of Jacob shall come he that shall have dominion, and shall destroy him that remaineth of the city.
texts.num.24.20: And when he looked on Amalek, he took up his parable, and said, Amalek was the first of the nations, but his latter end shall be that he shall perish for ever.
texts.num.24.21: And he looked on the Kenites, and took up his parable, and said, Strong is thy dwelling-place, and thou puttest thy nest in a rock.
texts.num.24.22: Nevertheless, the Kenite shall be wasted, until Asher shall carry thee away captive.
texts.num.24.23: And he took up his parable, and said, Alas, who shall live when God doeth this!
texts.num.24.24: And ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Ashur, and shall afflict Eber, and he also shall perish for ever.
texts.num.24.25: And Balaam arose, and went and returned to his place: and Balak also went his way.
texts.num.25.1: And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit lewdness with the daughters of Moab.
texts.num.25.2: And they called the people to the sacrifices of their gods: and the people ate, and bowed down to their gods.
texts.num.25.3: And Israel joined himself to Baal-peor: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel.
texts.num.25.4: And the LORD said to Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the LORD against the sun, that the fierce anger of the LORD may be turned away from Israel.
texts.num.25.5: And Moses said to the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined to Baal-peor.
texts.num.25.6: And, behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought to his brethren a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, who were weeping before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
texts.num.25.7: And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand;
texts.num.25.8: And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly: So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.
texts.num.25.9: And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.
texts.num.25.10: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.25.11: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, (while he was zealous for my sake among them,) that I consumed not the children of Israel in my jealousy.
texts.num.25.12: Wherefore say, Behold, I give to him my covenant of peace.
texts.num.25.13: And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his God, and made an atonement for the children of Israel.
texts.num.25.14: Now the name of the Israelite that was slain, even that was slain with the Midianitish woman, was Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites.
texts.num.25.15: And the name of the Midianitish woman that was slain was Cozbi the daughter of Zur; he was head over a people, and of a chief house in Midian.
texts.num.25.16: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
texts.num.25.17: Distress the Midianites, and smite them:
texts.num.25.18: For they distress you with their wiles, with which they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian their sister, who was slain in the day of the plague for Peor's sake.
texts.num.26.1: And it came to pass after the plague, that the LORD spoke to Moses, and to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, saying,
texts.num.26.2: Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, throughout their fathers' house, all that are able to go to war in Israel.
texts.num.26.3: And Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho, saying,
texts.num.26.4: Take the sum of the people, from twenty years old and upward; as the LORD commanded Moses and the children of Israel, who went forth from the land of Egypt.
texts.num.26.5: Reuben the eldest son of Israel: the children of Reuben; Hanoch, of whom cometh the family of the Hanochites: Of Phallu, the family of the Phalluites:
texts.num.26.6: Of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites: of Carmi, the family of the Carmites.
texts.num.26.7: These are the families of the Reubenites: and they that were numbered of them were forty and three thousand and seven hundred and thirty.
texts.num.26.8: And the sons of Phallu; Eliab.
texts.num.26.9: And the sons of Eliab; Nemuel, and Dathan, and Abiram. This is that Dathan and Abiram, who were famous in the congregation, who strove against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when they strove against the LORD:
texts.num.26.10: And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up together with Korah, when that company died, when the fire devoured two hundred and fifty men: and they became a sign.
texts.num.26.11: Notwithstanding the children of Korah died not.
texts.num.26.12: The sons of Simeon after their families: of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites: of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites: of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites:
texts.num.26.13: Of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites: of Shaul, the family of the Shaulites.
texts.num.26.14: These are the families of the Simeonites, twenty and two thousand and two hundred.
texts.num.26.15: The children of Gad after their families: of Zephon, the family of the Zephonites: of Haggai, the family of the Haggites: of Shuni, the family of the Shunites:
texts.num.26.16: Of Ozni, the family of the Oznites: of Eri, the family of the Erites:
texts.num.26.17: Of Arod, the family of the Arodites: of Areli, the family of the Arelites.
texts.num.26.18: These are the families of the children of Gad, according to those that were numbered of them, forty thousand and five hundred.
texts.num.26.19: The sons of Judah were Er and Onan: and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
