texts.num.4.11: And upon the altar of gold, shall they spread a wrapper of blue, and shall cover the same in a covering of badgers’ skin,—and shall put in the staves thereof,
texts.num.4.12: And they shall take all the utensils of attendance wherewith they attend in the sanctuary, and put them within a wrapper of blue, and cover the same in a covering of badgers’ skin,—and put them on a frame.
texts.num.4.13: Then shall they remove the fat-ashes from the altar,—and spread over it a wrapper of purple;
texts.num.4.14: and put thereupon all the utensils thereof wherewith they minister thereupon—the fire-pans, the flesh-hooks—and the shovels and the tossing-bowls, all the utensils of the altar,—and shall spread over it a covering of badgers’ skin and put in the staves thereof.
texts.num.4.15: So shall Aaron and his sons make an end of covering the sanctuary, and all the utensils of the sanctuary, when the camp is to set forward, then after that, shall the sons of Kohath enter to bear it, but they must not put forth a touch unto that which, is holy, else should they die, these, shall be the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting.
texts.num.4.16: But the care of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, [shall be] —the light-giving oil, and the fragrant incense, and the perpetual meal-offering, and the anointing oil, the care of all the habitation, and all that is therein, both as to the sanctuary, and as to the furniture thereof.
texts.num.4.17: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying:
texts.num.4.18: Do not let the tribe of the families of the Kohathites be cut off out of the midst of the Levites.
texts.num.4.19: This, therefore, do ye for them, so shall they live and not die when they approach the most holy place,—Aaron and his sons shall enter and set them man by man over his labour, and unto his burden;
texts.num.4.20: but they shall not enter to see, for a moment, that which is holy, else should they die.
texts.num.4.21: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.4.22: reckon up the sum of the sons of Gershon even of them also,—by their ancestral house by their families;
texts.num.4.23: from thirty years old and upwards even to fifty years, shalt thou number them,—All that may enter to take rank in the host, to do laborious work in the tent of meeting.
texts.num.4.24: This, shall be the labour of the families of the Gershonites,—in labouring and in bearing:
texts.num.4.25: they shall bear the curtains of the habitation and the tent of meeting, the covering thereof and the covering of badgers’ skin which is over above it,—and the screen, at the entrance of the tent of meeting;
texts.num.4.26: and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the entrance of the gate of the court which is near the habitation and near the altar round about, and their cords, and all their articles of service, and all that is to be done to them when they shall do their labour,
texts.num.4.27: At the bidding of Aaron and his sons, shall be all the labour of the sons of the Gershonites, to the extent of their every burden, and to the extent of all their labour,—so shall ye appoint unto them in charge their every burden.
texts.num.4.28: This, shall be the labour of the families of the sons of the Gershonites in the tent of meeting,—and, the charge of them, shall be in the hand of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
texts.num.4.29: As for the sons of Merari,—by their families by their ancestral house, shall ye number them;
texts.num.4.30: from thirty years old and upwards even to fifty years, shall ye number them,—all that enter into the host, to do laborious work in the tent of meeting,
texts.num.4.31: And, this, shall be their charge of the burdens, to the extent of all their labour in the tent of meeting, the boards of the habitation, and the bars thereof and he pillars thereof and the sockets thereof:
texts.num.4.32: and the pillars of the court round about and their sockets and their pins and their cords, to the extent of all their articles, to the extent of all their labour, and by names, shall ye put under their care the articles of their charge of burdens.
texts.num.4.33: This, shall be the labour of the families of the sons of Merari, to the extent of all their labour in the tent of meeting,—in the hand of Ithamar, son of Aaron, the priest.
texts.num.4.34: Then did Moses and Aaron, and the princes of the assembly, number the sons of the Kohathites, by their families, and by their ancestral house;
texts.num.4.35: from thirty years old and upwards, even unto fifty years old, all that might enter the host, to labour in the tent of meeting;
texts.num.4.36: and they who were numbered of them, by their families, were found to be two thousand, seven hundred and fifty.
texts.num.4.37: These, were they who were num-bered of the families of the Kohathites, all that might labour in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron did number, at the bidding of Yahweh by the mediation of Moses.
texts.num.4.38: And they who were numbered of the sons of Gershon,—by their families, and by their ancestral house;
texts.num.4.39: from thirty years old and upwards, even to fifty years old, all that might enter the host, to labour in the tent of meeting,:
texts.num.4.40: yea they who were numbered of them, by their families, by their ancestral house,—were found to be—two thousand, and six hundred, and thirty.
texts.num.4.41: These, are they who were numbered of the families of the sons of Gershon, all who might labour in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron did number, at the bidding of Yahweh.
texts.num.4.42: And they who were numbered of the families of the sons of Merari, by their families by their ancestral house;
texts.num.4.43: from thirty years old and upwards, even unto fifty years old,—all that might enter the host to labour in the tent of meeting;
texts.num.4.44: yea they who were numbered of them, by their families, were found to be—three thousand and two hundred.
texts.num.4.45: These, are they who were numbered of the families of the sons of Merari,—whom Moses and Aaron did number, at the bidding of Yahweh, by the mediation of Moses.
texts.num.4.46: All they who were numbered, whom Moses and Aaron and the princes of Israel did number, even the Levites, by their families and by their ancestral house;
texts.num.4.47: from thirty years old and upwards, even unto fifty years old, all that might enter, to toil in the work of labouring and in the work of bearing burdens, in the tent of meeting,
texts.num.4.48: yea, they who were numbered of them were found to be—eight thousand, and five hundred, and eighty.
texts.num.4.49: At the bidding of Yahweh, were they put in charge by the mediation of Moses, man by man, over his labour and over his burden,—yea, they who were put in charge by him, were they, whom Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.num.5.1: And Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying:—
texts.num.5.2: Command the sons of Israel, that they send forth out of the camp, every leper, and every one that hath a flux,—and every one that is unclean by the dead:
texts.num.5.3: whether male or female, ye shall send them forth, unto the outside of the camp, shall ye send them,—that they make not their camps unclean, in the midst whereof, I, have my habitation.
texts.num.5.4: And the sons of Israel did so, and sent them forth unto the outside of the camp,—as Yahweh spake unto Moses, so, did the sons of Israel.
texts.num.5.5: And Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.5.6: Speak unto the sons of Israel: When any man or woman, shall do aught of any human sin, in acting unfaithfully against Yahweh,—and that person shall become aware of his guilt,
texts.num.5.7: then shall they confess their sin which they have done, and he shall make good that wherein he is guilty, in the principal thereof, and the fifth part thereof, shall he add thereunto,—and give to him against whom he is guilty,
texts.num.5.8: But if one have no kinsman unto whom he may make good that wherein he is guilty, then that wherein he is guilty, which is to be restored to Yahweh, shall be the priest’s,—besides the ram of propitiation, wherewith a propitiatory-covering is to be put over him.
texts.num.5.9: And every heave-offering, of all the hallowed things of the sons of Israel which they bring near to the priest, unto him, shall it belong.
texts.num.5.10: And, every man’s hallowed things, shall be, his own,—what any man giveth to the priest, shall be his.
texts.num.5.11: And Yahweh spake unto Moses saying:
texts.num.5.12: Speak unto the sons of Israel, and thou shalt say unto them,—When any man’s wife, shall turn aside, and commit against him an act of unfaithfulness;
texts.num.5.13: and a man shall lie with her carnally, and it shall be concealed from the eyes of her husband and be kept close but, she, hath committed uncleanness,—though witness, there is none against her, and she, hath not been caught;
texts.num.5.14: but there shall pass over him a spirit of jealousy, and he shall become jealous of his wife, she having committed uncleanness,—or there shall pass over him a spirit of jealousy, and he shall become jealous of his wife, she not, having committed uncleanness,
texts.num.5.15: then shall the man bring in his wife unto the priest, and shall bring in her offering for her, the tenth of an ephah of the meal of barley,—he shall not pour thereon oil, nor put thereon frankincense, for a jealousy gift, it is, a reminding gift bringing to mind iniquity.
texts.num.5.16: Then shall the priest bring her near,—and cause her to stand before Yahweh;
texts.num.5.17: and the priest shall take hallowed water in an earthen vessel,—and of the dust which shall be upon the floor of the habitation, shall the priest take, and put into the water;
texts.num.5.18: and the priest shall cause the woman to stand before Yahweh, and shall bare the head of the woman, and shall place upon her hands the reminding gift, it being a jealousy gift,—and in the hand of the priest, shall be the deadly water that bringeth a curse;
texts.num.5.19: and the priest shall put her on oath and shall say unto the woman:—If no man hath lain with thee, and if thou hast not turned aside in uncleanness, [unto another] instead of thy husband, be thou clear from this deadly water that causeth a curse.
texts.num.5.20: But, if, thou, hast turned aside, [to another] instead of thy husband and if thou hast made thyself unclean,—in that a man hath known thee carnally, other than thy husband,
texts.num.5.21: then shall the priest put the woman on oath with an oath of cursing, and the priest shall say unto the woman, Yahweh give thee up for a curse and for an oath in the midst of thy people,—in that Yahweh shall give up thy thigh to fall away, and thy womb to swell:
texts.num.5.22: so shall this water that causeth a curse enter into thy body, causing womb to swell and thigh to fall away. And the woman shall say, Amen, Amen.
texts.num.5.23: Then shall the priest write these curses in a scroll,—and wipe them out into the deadly water;
texts.num.5.24: and shall cause the woman to drink the deadly water that causeth a curse,—and the deadly water that causeth a curse shall enter into her.
texts.num.5.25: Then shall the priest take from the hand of the woman the jealousy meal-offering,—and shall wave the meal-offering before Yahweh, and bring it near unto the altar;
texts.num.5.26: and the priest shall take a handful from the meal-offering, a remembrancer thereof, and make a perfume at the altar,—and afterwards, shall cause the woman to drink the water.
texts.num.5.27: And as soon as he causeth her to drink, the water, then shall it be, that, if she have fallen into uncleanness and committed unfaithfulness against her husband, as soon as the deadly water that causeth a curse hath entered into her, so soon shall her womb swell and her thigh fall away,—thus shall the woman become a curse in the midst of her people.
texts.num.5.28: But, if the woman have not fallen into uncleanness, but is pure, then shall she be clear and shall bear seed.
texts.num.5.29: This, is the law of jealousies,—when a wife shall turn aside [to another] instead of her husband, and fall into uncleanness;
texts.num.5.30: or when there passeth over, a husband, a spirit of jealousy, and he becometh jealous of his wife, then shall he cause the woman to stand before Yahweh, and the priest shall execute upon her all this law:
texts.num.5.31: thus shall the man be clear of iniquity; but that woman, shall bear her iniquity.
texts.num.6.1: And Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.6.2: Speak unto the sons of Israel, and thou shalt say unto them,—When any man or woman, would make the special vow of One Separate, by separating himself unto Yahweh,
texts.num.6.3: from wine and strong drink, shall he separate himself, neither vinegar of wine nor vinegar of strong drink, shall he drink,—and no liquor of grapes, shall he drink, no grapes fresh or dried, shall he eat.
texts.num.6.4: All the days of his separation, of nothing that is made from the grapevine from the seeds even to the skin, shall he eat.
texts.num.6.5: All the days of his vow of separation, no razor, shall pass over his head,—until the days are fulfilled for which he shall separate himself to Yahweh hallowed, shall he be, letting the locks of the hair of his head grow long.
texts.num.6.6: All the days for which he hath separated himself unto Yahweh to no dead person, shall he go in.
texts.num.6.7: Neither for his father nor for his mother nor for his brother nor for his sister, shall he make himself unclean-not even for them, should they die,—because, his separation unto God, is upon his head,
texts.num.6.8: All his days of separation hallowed, is he unto Yahweh.
texts.num.6.9: But if one that is dying should die by him in a moment suddenly, then shall he count unclean his head of separation,—and shall shave his head, on the day he cleanseth himself, on the seventh day, shall he shave it.
texts.num.6.10: And on the eighth day, shall he bring in. two turtle-doves, or two young pigeons,—unto the priest, unto the entrance of the tent of meeting;
texts.num.6.11: and the priest shall make, of one a sin—bearer and of one an ascending-sacrifice, and so put a propitiatory-covering over him, for that he sinned in respect of the dead person,—thus shall he hallow his head on that day.
texts.num.6.12: Then shall he separate unto Yahweh his days of separation, and shall bring in a he-lamb a year old as a guilt-bearer,—and, the first days, shall be lost because his separation, was made unclean.
texts.num.6.13: And, this, is the law of the Separate One, on the day when he fulfilleth his days of separation, he shall be brought in unto the entrance of the tent of meeting:
texts.num.6.14: then shall he bring near as his offering unto Yahweh.—one he-lamb a year old, without defect for an ascending-sacrifice, and one ewe-lamb a year old without defect for a sin-bearer,—and one ram, without defect for a peace-offering;
texts.num.6.15: and a basket of unleavened cakes—fine meal in round cakes overflowed with oil, and thin cakes of unleavened bread, anointed with oil,—with their meal-offering and their drink-offerings.
texts.num.6.16: Then shall the priest bring [them] near before Yahweh,—and offer his sin-bearer and his ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.6.17: and the ram, shall he offer as a peace-offering unto Yahweh, besides the basket of unleavened cakes,—and the priest shall offer the meal-offering thereof and the drink-offering thereof,
texts.num.6.18: Then shall the Separate One shave, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, his head of separation,—and take the hair of his head of separation, and put upon the fire, which is under the peace-offering.
texts.num.6.19: Then shall the priest take the shoulder for boiling from the ram, and one unleavened round cake from the basket, and one unleavened thin cake,—and place them on the hands, of the Separate One after he hath shaven off his [hair of] separation;
texts.num.6.20: and the priest shall wave them as a wave-offering before Yahweh, hallowed, it is for the priest, besides the wave breast, and besides the heave leg,—and, afterwards, may the Separate One drink wine.
texts.num.6.21: This is the law of One Separate what he shall vow, his offering unto Yahweh with respect to his separation, besides what his hand may obtain: as required by the vow that he shall vow, so, must he do, with respect to the law of his separation.
texts.num.6.22: And Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.6.23: Speak unto Aaron, and unto his sons saying Thus, shall ye bless the sons of Israel,—saying unto them:
texts.num.6.24: Yahweh bless thee, and keep thee:
texts.num.6.25: Yahweh cause his face to shine upon thee and be gracious unto thee:
texts.num.6.26: Yahweh lift up his face unto thee, and appoint unto thee peace.
texts.num.6.27: Thus shall they put my name upon the sons of Israel,—and, I, myself, will bless them.
texts.num.7.1: And it came to pass, on the day when Moses made an end of rearing up the habitation and anointing it, and hallowing it, and all the furniture thereof, and the altar, and all the utensils thereof,—both of anointing them, and hallowing them,
texts.num.7.2: that the princes of Israel, the heads of their ancestral houses, made an offering,—they being princes of the tribes, they being the men who stood over them who were numbered:
texts.num.7.3: yea then brought they in as their offering, before Yahweh—six covered waggons, and twelve oxen, a waggon for every two of the princes and an ox for each one,—yea they brought them near before the habitation.
texts.num.7.4: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.7.5: Take [them] of them, so shall they be for doing the laborious work of the tent of meeting,—and thou shalt give them unto the Levites, to every man according to the need of his laborious work.
texts.num.7.6: So Moses took the waggons, and the oxen,—and gave them unto the Levites:
texts.num.7.7: two of the waggons and four of the oxen, gave he unto the sons of Gershon,—according to the need of their laborious work;
texts.num.7.8: and four of the waggons, and eight of the oxen, gave he unto the sons of Merari,—according to the need of their laborious work, in the hand of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest;
texts.num.7.9: but, unto the sons of Kohath, gave he none,—because as to the laborious work of the sanctuary which pertained unto them, upon their shoulders, were they to carry it.
texts.num.7.10: So then the princes offered for the dedication of the altar, on the day it was anointed,—yea the princes offered their oblation before the altar,
texts.num.7.11: And Yahweh said unto Moses: Each prince on his appointed day, thus shall they offer their oblation, for the dedication of the altar.
texts.num.7.12: And so it was, that, he who on the first day, offered his oblation,—was Nahshon son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah;
texts.num.7.13: and his offering, was—one charger of silver, a hundred and thirty shekels, the weight thereof, one tossing bowl of silver, seventy shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary,—both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil for a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.14: one spoon of ten shekels of gold full of incense;
texts.num.7.15: one choice young bullock one ram one he-lamb of the first year, as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.16: one young he-goat, as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.17: and as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Nashon, son of Amminadab.
texts.num.7.18: On the second day, Nethanel, son of Zuar, prince of Issachar, brought his offering.
texts.num.7.19: He offered as his oblation—one charger of silver, a hundred and thirty shekels, the weight thereof, one tossing bowl of silver, seventy shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary,—both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.20: one spoon of ten [shekels] of gold full of incense;
texts.num.7.21: one choice young bullock one ram one he-lamb of the first year, as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.22: one young he-goat, as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.23: and, as peace-offering two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Nethanel, son of Zuar.
texts.num.7.24: On the third day, the prince of the sons of Zebulun,—Eliab, son of Helon:
texts.num.7.25: his offering,—one charger of silver a hundred and thirty shekels, the weight thereof, one tossing bowl of silver, seventy shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary,—both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.26: one spoon, of ten [shekels] of gold full of incense;
texts.num.7.27: one choice young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.28: one young he-goat, as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.29: and as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Eliab, son of Helon.
texts.num.7.30: On the fourth day, the prince of he sons of Reuben,—Elizur, son of Shedeur:
texts.num.7.31: his offering, one charger of silver, a hundred and thirty [shekels], the weight thereof, one tossing bowl of Silver, seventy shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary,—both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil, as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.32: one spoon of ten [shekels] of gold full of incense:
texts.num.7.33: one choice young bullock one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.34: one young he-goat for a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.35: and as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Elizur, son of Shedeur.
texts.num.7.36: On the fifth day, the prince of the sons of Simeon,—Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai:
texts.num.7.37: his offering, one charger of silver a hundred and thirty shekels, the weight thereof, one tossing bowl of silver, seventy shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.38: one spoon of ten [shekels] of gold, full of incense;
texts.num.7.39: one choice young bullock one ram one he-lamb of the first year as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.40: one young he-goat as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.41: and, as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai.
texts.num.7.42: On the sixth day, the prince of the sons of Gad,—Eliasaph, son of Deuel:
texts.num.7.43: his offering, one charger of silver, a hundred and thirty [shekels], the weight thereof, one tossing bowl, of silver, seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary,—both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil, as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.44: one spoon of ten [shekels] of gold full of incense;
texts.num.7.45: one choice young bullock one ram one he-lamb of the first year, as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.46: one young he-goat as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.47: and as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Eliasaph, son of Deuel.
texts.num.7.48: On the seventh day, the prince of the sons of Ephraim,—Elishama, son of Ammihud:
texts.num.7.49: his offering, one charger of silver a hundred and thirty shekels, the weight thereof, one tossing bowl of silver, seventy shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary,—both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.50: one spoon of ten [shekels] of gold, full of incense;
texts.num.7.51: one choice young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.52: one young he-goat, as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.53: and as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Elishama, son of Ammihud.
texts.num.7.54: On the eighth day, the prince of the sons of Manasseh,—Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur:
texts.num.7.55: his offering, one charger of silver, a hundred and thirty [shekels], the weight thereof, one tossing bowl, of silver, seventy shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary,—both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.56: one spoon of ten [shekels] of gold full of incense;
texts.num.7.57: one choice young bullock one ram one he-lamb of the first year as an ascending-sacrifice:
texts.num.7.58: one young he-goat, as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.59: and as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
texts.num.7.60: On the ninth day, the prince of the sons of Benjamin,—Abidan, son of Gideoni:
texts.num.7.61: his offering, one charger of silver, a hundred and thirty [shekels], the weight thereof,—one tossing bowl of silver, seventy shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary,—both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil, as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.62: one spoon, of ten [shekels] of gold full of incense;
texts.num.7.63: one choice young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.64: one young he-goat as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.65: and as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Abidan, son of Gideoni.
texts.num.7.66: On the tenth day, the prince of the sons of Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai:
texts.num.7.67: his offering, one charger of silver a hundred and thirty [shekels], the weight thereof,—one tossing bowl of silver, seventy shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary,—both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.68: one spoon, of ten [shekels] of gold, full of incense;
texts.num.7.69: one choice young bullock one ram one he-lamb of the first year as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.70: one young he-goat, as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.71: and as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai.
texts.num.7.72: On the eleventh day, the prince of the sons of Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran;
texts.num.7.73: his offering, one charger of silver, a hundred and thirty [shekels], the weight thereof, one tossing bowl, of silver, seventy shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary,—both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.74: one spoon of ten [shekels] of gold, full of incense;
texts.num.7.75: one choice young bullock, one ram one he-lamb of the first year, as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.76: one young he-goat, as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.77: and as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering of Pagiel, son of Ochran.
texts.num.7.78: On the twelfth day, the prince of the sons of Naphtali, Ahira, son of Enan:
texts.num.7.79: his offering, one charger of silver a hundred and thirty [shekels], the weight thereof, one tossing bowl of silver, seventy shekels by the shekel of the sanctuary, both of them, full of fine meal overflowed with oil, as a meal-offering;
texts.num.7.80: one spoon of ten [shekels] of gold full of incense;
texts.num.7.81: one choice young bullock one ram one he-lamb of the first year, as an ascending-sacrifice;
texts.num.7.82: one young he-goat as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.7.83: and, as a peace-offering, two oxen, five rams five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year, this, was the offering of Ahira, son of Enan.
texts.num.7.84: This, was the offering for the dedication of the altar in the day when it was anointed, from the princes of Israel,—twelve chargers of silver twelve tossing bowls of silver, twelve spoons of gold;
texts.num.7.85: a hundred and thirty [shekels], each charger of silver, and seventy, each tossing bowl,—all the silver of the vessels, two thousand and four hundred [shekels], by the shekel of the sanctuary;
texts.num.7.86: twelve spoons of gold full of incense, ten shekels each spoon by the shekel of the sanctuary,—all the gold of the spoons, a hundred and twenty [shekels].
texts.num.7.87: All the herd for the ascending-sacrifice,—twelve bullocks twelve rams twelve he-lambs of the first year with their meal-offering,—twelve young he-goats for the bearing of sin;
texts.num.7.88: and all the herd for the peace-offering, twenty-four bullocks sixty rams, sixty he-goats sixty he-lambs of the first year,—this, was the offering for the dedication of the altar, after it was anointed.
texts.num.7.89: And when Moses entered into the tent of meeting, that He might speak with him, then heard he the Voice speaking unto him from off the propitiatory that was upon the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim,—so He spake unto him.
texts.num.8.1: And Yahweh spake unto Moses saying:
texts.num.8.2: Speak unto Aaron, and thou shalt say unto him,—When thou lightest up the lamps, over against the front of the lampstand, shall the seven lamps give light.
texts.num.8.3: And Aaron did so, over against the front of the lampstand, lighted he up the lamps thereof,—As Yahweh commanded Moses,
texts.num.8.4: Now, this, was the work of the lampstand—beaten work of gold both in the shaft thereof and in the flowers thereof, was it beaten work, according to the appearance which Yahweh caused to appear unto Moses, so, made he the lampstand.
texts.num.8.5: And Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.8.6: Take the Levites, out of the midst of the sons of Israel,—and thou shalt purify them.
texts.num.8.7: And, thus, shalt thou do unto them, to purify them, sprinkle upon them sin-cleansing water,—then shall they, cause a razor to pass over all their flesh, and shall wash their clothes and so make themselves pure.
texts.num.8.8: Then shall they take a choice young bullock, with the meal-offering thereof even fine meal overflowed with oil,—and a second choice young bullock, shalt thou take. as a sin-bearer.
texts.num.8.9: Then shalt thou bring the Levites near, before the tent of meeting,—and shalt call together all the assembly of the sons of Israel;
texts.num.8.10: and shalt bring the Levites near before Yahweh,—and the sons of Israel shall lean their hands upon the Levites;
texts.num.8.11: and Aaron shall offer the Levites as a wave-offering before Yahweh, from among the sons of Israel,—so shall they be for performing the laborious work of Yahweh.
texts.num.8.12: And, the Levites, shall lean their hands upon the head of the bullocks; then make thou of the one a sin-bearer and of the other an ascending-sacrifice unto Yahweh, to put a propitiatory-covering over the Levites.
texts.num.8.13: Thus shalt thou cause the Levites to stand before Aaron and before his sons,—thus shalt thou offer them as a wave-offering unto Yahweh;
texts.num.8.14: thus shalt thou separate the Levites out of the midst of the sons of Israel,—thus shall the Levites become mine.
texts.num.8.15: And after that, shall the Levites enter to do the labour of the tent of meeting,—so shalt thou purify them, and offer them as a wave-offering,
texts.num.8.16: For, given, given, they are unto me, out of the midst of the sons of Israel,—instead of every firstborn that a mother beareth from among the sons of Israel, have I taken them unto me.
texts.num.8.17: For mine, is every firstborn among the sons of Israel, among men and among beasts,—on the day when I smote every firstborn in the land of Egypt, did I hallow them unto me.
texts.num.8.18: Therefore have I taken the Levites,—instead of every firstborn among the sons of Israel;
texts.num.8.19: therefore have I given the Levites as a gift unto Aaron and unto his sons, out of the midst of the sons of Israel, to do the laborious work of the sons of Israel in the tent of meeting, and to put a propitiatory-covering over the sons of Israel,—so shall there be among the sons of Israel, no plague, by the coming nigh of the sons of Israel unto the sanctuary.
texts.num.8.20: And Moses and Aaron and all the assembly of the sons of Israel did thus unto the Levites,—according to all that Yahweh commanded Moses as touching the Levites, so, did the sons of Israel unto them.
texts.num.8.21: And the Levites accepted the cleansing from sin and washed their clothes, and Aaron offered them as a wave-offering before Yahweh,—and Aaron put a propitiatory-covering over them to make them pure.
texts.num.8.22: And after that, went the Levites in to do their laborious work in the tent of meeting, before Aaron and before his sons,—as Yahweh commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so, did they unto them.
texts.num.8.23: And Yahweh spake unto Moses saying;
texts.num.8.24: This is what concerneth the Levites,—from twenty-five years old and upwards, shall they enter to take rank in the host, for doing the laborious work of the tent of meeting;
texts.num.8.25: but from the age of fifty years, shall they retire from taking rank in the labour, and shall do laborious work no more;
texts.num.8.26: yet shall they wait upon their brethren in the tent of meeting, by keeping charge, but laborious work, shall they not perform,—thus, shalt thou do unto the Levites, as touching their charges.
texts.num.9.1: And Yahweh spake unto Moses in the desert of Sinai, in the second year by their coming forth out of the land of Egypt in the first month, saying:
texts.num.9.2: Let the sons of Israel therefore, keep the passover in its appointed season:
texts.num.9.3: on the fourteenth day of this month between the two evenings, shall ye keep it, in its appointed season,—according to all the statute thereof and according to all the regulations thereof, shall ye keep it.
texts.num.9.4: Then spake Moses unto the sons of Israel that they should keep the passover.
texts.num.9.5: So they kept the passover in the first [month], on the fourteenth day of the month between the two evenings, in the desert of Sinai,—according to all that Yahweh commanded Moses, so, did the sons of Israel.
texts.num.9.6: But so it was that there were, certain men who had become unclean by a dead person, and could not keep the passover on that day,—therefore came they near before Moses and before Aaron on that day.
texts.num.9.7: Then said those men unto him, We, are unclean by a dead person,—wherefore should we become of less esteem for want of offering the oblation of Yahweh in its appointed season, in the midst of the sons of Israel?
texts.num.9.8: And Moses said unto them,—Stay, and let me hear, what Yahweh shall command concerning you!
texts.num.9.9: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.9.10: Speak unto the sons of Israel, saying,—Though, any man, be unclean by a dead person or be on a journey afar off, whether in the case of yourselves or of your generations, yet shall he keep a passover unto Yahweh.
texts.num.9.11: In the second month, on the fourteenth day between the two evenings, shall they keep it,—with unleavened cakes and bitter herbs, shall they eat it.
texts.num.9.12: They shall not leave thereof until morning, and no bone, shall they break therein—according to all the statutes of the passover, shall they keep it.
texts.num.9.13: But as for the man who is, clean, and no a journey, doth not chance to be and yet faileth to keep the passover, that person shall he cut off from among his kinsfolk,—for the oblation of Yahweh, hath he not offered in its appointed season, his own sin, shall, that man, bear.
texts.num.9.14: When moreover there may sojourn with you a sojourner, who would keep a passover unto Yahweh, according to the statute of the passover, and according to the regulation thereof, so, must he keep [it],—one statute, shall there be for you, both for the sojourner and for the native of the land.
texts.num.9.15: Now, on the day the habitation was reared, the cloud covered the habitation, even the tent of the testimony,—and in the evening, it was over the habitation, like an appearance of fire, until morning,
texts.num.9.16: Thus, came it to pass continually, the cloud, covered it,—and an appearance of fire, by night;
texts.num.9.17: but at the bidding of the upgoings of the cloud from off the tent, then, after that, the sons of Israel set forward,—and in the place where the cloud abode, there the sons of Israel encamped:
texts.num.9.18: at the bidding of Yahweh, the sons of Israel set forward, and at the bidding of Yahweh, they encamped,—all the days that the cloud abode upon the habitation, they remained encamped.
texts.num.9.19: And when the cloud lengthened out its stay upon the habitation, many days, then would the sons of Israel keep the watch of Yahweh, and would not set forward.
texts.num.9.20: And, so it was, when the cloud would be a few days upon the habitation, at the bidding of Yahweh, they remained encamped, and at the bidding of Yahweh, they set forward.
texts.num.9.21: And, so it was, when the cloud would be from evening until morning, as soon as the cloud went up in the morning, so soon did they set forward: whether by day or by night, as soon as the cloud went up, so soon did they set forward.
texts.num.9.22: Whether for two days or a month or a year, the cloud lengthened out its stay upon the habitation abiding thereupon, the sons of Israel remained encamped and set not forward,—but at the upgoings thereof, they set forward.
texts.num.9.23: At the bidding of Yahweh, they encamped, and at the bidding of Yahweh, they set forward,—the watch of Yahweh, they kept, at the bidding of Yahweh by the hand of Moses.
texts.num.10.1: And Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.10.2: Make thee two trumpets of silver, of beaten work, shalt thou make them,—and they shall be unto thee for calling the assembly, and for setting forward the camps.
texts.num.10.3: As soon as they blow therewith, so soon shall all the assembly assemble themselves unto thee, unto the entrance of the tent of meeting.
texts.num.10.4: And, if, only once, they blow, then shall the princes, the heads of the thousands of Israel, gather themselves unto thee.
texts.num.10.5: But when ye blow an alarm, then shall set forward the camps that are encamped eastwards;
texts.num.10.6: and when ye blow a second alarm, then shall set forward the camps that are encamped southwards,—an alarm, shall they blow for setting them forward,
texts.num.10.7: But in calling together the convocation, ye shall blow but shall not sound an alarm.
texts.num.10.8: And, the sons of Aaron the priests, shall blow with the trumpets,—and it shall be unto you for a statute age-abiding, unto your generations.
texts.num.10.9: And when ye go into war in your land against the assailant that assaileth you, then shall ye blow an alarm with the trumpets,—and bring yourselves to mind before Yahweh your God, and be saved, from your enemies,
texts.num.10.10: And in your day of rejoicing and in your appointed seasons and in the beginnings of your months, then shall ye blow with the trumpets, over your ascending-sacrifices, and over your peace-offerings,—so shall they be unto you for a memorial before your God. I—Yahweh, am your God.
texts.num.10.11: And so it came to pass in the second year, in the second month on the twentieth of the month, that the cloud lifted itself up, from off the habitation of the testimony;
texts.num.10.12: and the sons of Israel set forward by their removals from the desert of Sinai, and then the cloud abode in the desert of Paran.
texts.num.10.13: Thus then did they set forward for the first time,—at the bidding of Yahweh, by the hand of Moses.
texts.num.10.14: So the standard of the camp of the sons of Judah set forward first, by their hosts, and over his own host, was Nahshon, son of Amminadab;
texts.num.10.15: and, over the host of the tribe of the sons of Issachar, Nethanel, son of Zuar;
texts.num.10.16: and, over the host of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab, son of Helon.
texts.num.10.17: Then was taken down the habitation,—and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari set forward bearing the habitation.
texts.num.10.18: Then set forward the standard of the camp of Reuben, by their hosts,—and over his own host, Elizur, son of Shedeur;
texts.num.10.19: and, over the host of the tribe of the sons of Simeon, Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai;
texts.num.10.20: and, over the host of the tribe of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph, son of Deuel.
texts.num.10.21: Then set forward the Kohathites, bearing the sanctuary,—and so the habitation was reared by the time they came in.
texts.num.10.22: Then set forward the standard of the camp of the sons of Ephraim by their hosts,—and over his own host, was Elishama son of Ammihud;
texts.num.10.23: and, over the host of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur;
texts.num.10.24: and, over the host of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, Abidan, son of Gideoni.
texts.num.10.25: Then set forward the standard of the camp of the sons of Dan, bringing up the rear of all the camps, by their hosts,—and over his own host, Ahiezur, son of Ammishaddai;
texts.num.10.26: and, over the host of the tribe of the sons of Asher, Pagiel, son of Ochran;
texts.num.10.27: and, over the host of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, Ahira, son of Enan.
texts.num.10.28: These, were the settings-forward of the sons of Israel by their hosts,—thus did they set forward.
texts.num.10.29: Then said Moses to Hobab, son of Raguel the Midianite, father-in-law of Moses: Setting forward, are we unto the place of which Yahweh hath said, The same, will I give unto you,—Oh come with us and we will do thee good, for, Yahweh, hath spoken good, concerning Israel.
texts.num.10.30: And he said unto him, I will not go,—but unto my own land, and unto my own kindred, will I go.
texts.num.10.31: Then said he: I beseech thee, do not forsake us,—for, on this account, hast thou come to know of our encamping in the desert, so shalt thou be unto us as eyes;
texts.num.10.32: and it shall be if thou wilt go with us,—yea it shall be that with the very good wherewith Yahweh shall do us good, will we do good unto thee.
texts.num.10.33: So then they went forward, from the mountain of Yahweh, a journey of three days,—and the ark of the covenant of Yahweh, was going before them a journey of three days, to search out for them a resting-place,
texts.num.10.34: And the cloud of Yahweh, was over them by day,—when they set forward out of the camp.
texts.num.10.35: And it came to pass when the ark set forward, that Moses said: Arise, O Yahweh! and scattered be thy foes, Let them that hate thee flee before thee;
texts.num.10.36: But when it rested, he said,—Return, O Yahweh! unto the myriads of the thousands of Israel.
texts.num.11.1: And it came to pass that when the people were giving themselves up to murmuring, it was grievous in the ears of Yahweh,—so Yahweh hearkened, and kindled was his anger, and the fire of Yahweh burned among them, and consumed the uttermost part of the camp.
texts.num.11.2: Then did the people make outcry unto Moses,—and Moses prayed unto Yahweh, and the fire sank down.
texts.num.11.3: So he called the name of that place, Taberah [="A Burning"] because there burned among them the fire of Yahweh.
texts.num.11.4: Moreover the mixed multitude that was in their midst concealed not their lusting,—and so even the sons of Israel, fell away and wept, and said: Who will grant us to eat flesh?
texts.num.11.5: We remember the fish that we did eat in Egypt, without money,—the cucumbers, and the water-melons, and the leeks and the onions, and the garlick.
texts.num.11.6: But, now, our soul is dried up, there is nothing at all,—unless, unto the manna, [we turn] our eyes.
texts.num.11.7: Now, the manna, was like coriander seed, and the appearance thereof like the appearance of bdellium,
texts.num.11.8: The people used to go about and pick it up, and grind it with a pair of mill-stones, or pound it in a mortar, and boil it in a pot, and make it into round cakes,—then was the taste thereof like the taste of a sweet cake made with oil.
texts.num.11.9: When the dew came down upon the camp by night, the manna came down thereupon.
texts.num.11.10: So then Moses heard the people weeping by their families, every one at the entrance of his tent,—then kindled the anger of Yahweh fiercely, and in the eyes of Moses, it was grievous.
texts.num.11.11: And Moses said unto Yahweh—Wherefore hast thou let thy servant come to grief, and wherefore have I not found favour in thine eyes,—that thou shouldest lay the burden of all this people upon me?
texts.num.11.12: Did, I, conceive all this people, or, I, beget them,—that thou shouldest say unto me, Carry them in thy bosom, as a nursing father carrieth a suckling, unto the soil which thou didst swear unto their fathers?
texts.num.11.13: Whence should, I, have flesh to give to all this people,—for they keep weeping by me saying, Oh give us flesh that we may eat!
texts.num.11.14: Unable, am, I, by myself, to carry all this people,—for they are too heavy for me.
texts.num.11.15: But if, in this way, thou art going to deal with me, slay me, I beseech thee, slay, if I have found favour in thine eyes,—and let me not see my grief,
texts.num.11.16: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Gather thou unto me seventy men, from among the elders of Israel, of whom thou knowest that they are elders of the people and their overseers,—then shalt thou take them unto the tent of meeting, and they shall station themselves there with thee.
texts.num.11.17: Then will I come down, and speak with thee there, and will take of the spirit that is upon thee and put upon them,—and they shall carry, with thee, the burden of the people, and, thou, shalt not carry it by thyself.
texts.num.11.18: And, unto the people, shalt thou say: Hallow yourselves by to-morrow, and ye shall eat flesh, for ye have wept in the ears of Yahweh saying—Who will grant us to eat flesh? for it was well with us in Egypt,—so then Yahweh will give you flesh and ye shall eat.
texts.num.11.19: Not one day, shall ye eat nor two days,—nor five days nor ten days, nor twenty days:
texts.num.11.20: for a month of days until it cometh forth out of your nostrils, so shall it become to you a loathsome thing,—because ye have refused Yahweh who is in your midst, and have wept before him, saying, Wherefore now came we forth out of Egypt?
texts.num.11.21: And Moses said, Six hundred thousand footmen, are the people in whose midst am, I, yet thou hast said—Flesh, will I give unto them, and they shall eat for a month of days.
texts.num.11.22: Shall the flocks and herds, be slaughtered for them, that it may suffice for them? Shall all the fishes of the sea, be gathered together unto them that it may suffice for them?
texts.num.11.23: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, Shall the hand of Yahweh, fail? Now, shalt thou see whether my word come to pass unto thee or not.
texts.num.11.24: And Moses went forth and spake unto the people the words of Yahweh,—and gathered together seventy men from among the elders of the people, and caused them to stand round about the tent.
texts.num.11.25: Then Yahweh came down, in the cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the spirit that was upon him, and gave unto the seventy men—the elders. And it came to pass that when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and then did so no more.
texts.num.11.26: Now there were two men left behind in the camp—the name of the one, was Eldad and the name of the other, Medad, so then the spirit, rested on them—they, being among them who were written, though they had not gone forth unto the tent,—but they prophesied in the camp.
texts.num.11.27: And there ran a young man, and told Moses and said,—Eldad and Medad, are prophesying in the camp!
texts.num.11.28: Then responded Joshua son of Nun the attendant of Moses from his youth, and said,—My lord Moses forbid them!
texts.num.11.29: But Moses said unto him, Art, thou, jealous for, me? Oh would that, all the people of Yahweh, were prophets! Yea let Yahweh put his spirit upon them!
texts.num.11.30: Then was Moses received back into the camp,—he and the elders of Israel.
texts.num.11.31: Now, a wind, had sprung up, from Yahweh, and cut off quails from the sea, and let them lie over the camp—as it were a days journey here and a days journey there, round about the camp,—and as it were two cubits on the face of the land.
texts.num.11.32: And the people rose up all that day and all the night and all the next day, and gathered the quails, he that did least, gathered ten homers,—and they spread them out for themselves spreading away, round about the camp.
texts.num.11.33: The flesh, was yet between their teeth, not yet chewed,—when the anger of Yahweh, had kindled upon the people, and Yahweh smote the people, with an exceeding great plague.
texts.num.11.34: And the name of that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah—because there, they buried the people who had lusted,
texts.num.11.35: From Kibroth-hattaavah, the people set forward to Hazeroth,—and they remained in Hazeroth.
texts.num.12.1: And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses, on account of the Cushite woman whom he had taken,—for, a Cushite woman, had he taken.
texts.num.12.2: And they said: Is it only and solely with Moses, that Yahweh hath spoken? With us also, hath he not spoken? And Yahweh heard it.
texts.num.12.3: Now, the man Moses, was patient, exceedingly,—above all the sons of earth, who were on the face of the ground.
texts.num.12.4: Then said Yahweh suddenly, unto Moses, and unto Aaron, and unto Miriam, Come out ye three unto the tent of meeting. And they three went out.
texts.num.12.5: Then Yahweh came down in a pillar of cloud, and stood at the entrance of the tent,—and called Aaron and Miriam, and they both went forth.
texts.num.12.6: Then said he Hear, I beseech you my words. When ye have your prophet, As Yahweh in a vision, will I make myself known, unto him; In a dream, will I speak with him.
texts.num.12.7: Not so, my servant Moses,—In all my house, trusty, is he:
texts.num.12.8: Mouth to mouth, do I speak with him And plainly—not in dark sayings, And the form of Yahweh, doth he discern,—Wherefore then, were ye not afraid to speak against my servant—against Moses?
texts.num.12.9: And the anger of Yahweh kindled upon them and he departed.
texts.num.12.10: And, when, the cloud, removed from off the tent,—lo! Miriam, leprous, like snow! And Aaron turned unto Miriam and lo! …leprous!
texts.num.12.11: Then said Aaron unto Moses,—Oh my lord, do not I beseech thee lay upon us sin, although we have made ourselves foolish, and although we have sinned.
texts.num.12.12: Let her not, I beseech thee, remain like the still-born,—which when it is born of its mother, the half of its flesh is consumed.
texts.num.12.13: Then Moses made outcry unto Yahweh, saying,—O GOD, I beseech thee grant healing. I beseech thee unto her.
texts.num.12.14: And Yahweh said unto Moses: If, her own father, had, but spat, in her face, would she not, have acknowledged the shame for seven days? Let her shut herself up for seven days, outside the camp, and afterwards, let her be received back.
texts.num.12.15: So Miriam shut herself up, outside the camp, for seven days,—and, the people, set not forward, until Miriam had been received back.
texts.num.12.16: Then afterwards, did the people set forward from Hazeroth, and encamped in the desert of Paran.
texts.num.13.1: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.13.2: Send for thee men and let them spy out the land of Canaan, which I am giving unto the sons of Israel,—one man each for the tribe of his fathers, shalt thou send, each one a prince among them.
texts.num.13.3: So then Moses sent them out of the desert of Paran, at the bidding of Yahweh,—all of them, great men, heads of the sons of Israel, were they.
texts.num.13.4: And, these, are their names,—Of the tribe of Reuben, Shammua, son of Zaccur;
texts.num.13.5: Of the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat, son of Hori;
texts.num.13.6: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb, son of Jephunneh;
texts.num.13.7: Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal, son of Joseph;
texts.num.13.8: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea, son of Nun;
texts.num.13.9: Of the tribe of Benjamin, Palti, son of Raphu;
texts.num.13.10: Of the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel, son of Sodi;
texts.num.13.11: Of the tribe of Joseph—of the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
texts.num.13.12: Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel, son of Gemalli;
texts.num.13.13: Of the tribe of Asher, Sethur, son of Michael;
texts.num.13.14: Of the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi, son of Vophsi;
texts.num.13.15: Of the tribe of Gad, Geuel, son of Machi.
texts.num.13.16: These, are the names of the men, whom Moses sent to spy out the land,—but Moses called Hoshea son of Nun, Joshua.
texts.num.13.17: So Moses sent them, to spy out the land of Canaan,—and said unto them—Go up, here in the South, Yea ye shall go up the mountain;
texts.num.13.18: And shall see the land, what it is,—And the people that dwell thereupon, Whether they are, strong, or weak, Whether they are, few or many;
texts.num.13.19: And what, the land, is, wherein they dwell, Whether it is, good, or, bad,—And the cities within which they dwell, Whether in camps or in strongholds;
texts.num.13.20: And what the land is, Whether, fat, or, lean, Whether there is timber therein or is not, Then shall ye pluck up courage and take of the fruit of the land. Now the days, were the days of the first-fruits of grapes.
texts.num.13.21: So they went up, and spied out the land,—from the wilderness of Zin unto Rehob at the entering in of Hamath.
texts.num.13.22: Yea they went up in the South and entered as far as Hebron, and there, were Ahiman Sheshai and Talmai descendants of the Anak. Now, Hebron, was built seven years, before Zoan of Egypt.
texts.num.13.23: And they entered as far as the ravine of Eschol, and cut down, from thence a branch with one cluster of grapes, and bare it on a pole between two,—also of the pomegranates and of the figs.
texts.num.13.24: That place, was called, The Ravine of Eschol [="Cluster-ravine"]—on account of the cluster, which was cut down from thence by the sons of Israel.
texts.num.13.25: And they returned from spying out the land,—at the end of forty days.
texts.num.13.26: So they took their journey, and came in unto Moses and unto Aaron and unto all the assembly of the sons of Israel into the wilderness of Paran, towards Kadesh,—and brought back word—unto them and unto all the assembly, and showed them the fruit of the land.
texts.num.13.27: And they recounted unto him, and said, We entered into the land whither thou didst send us, and surely it doth flow with milk and honey, and, this, is the fruit thereof.
texts.num.13.28: Nevertheless surely mighty, are the people that dwell in the land,—and, the cities, walled in, exceeding great, moreover also, the descendants of the Anak, saw we there.
texts.num.13.29: Amalek, dwelleth in the land of the South; And, the Hittite, and the Jebusite and the Amorite, dwell in the mountain And the Canaanite, dwelleth by the sea, and by the side of the Jordan.
texts.num.13.30: And Caleb stilled the people unto Moses,—and said unto them—Let us go straight up, and possess it, for we shall, surely prevail, against it.
texts.num.13.31: But the men who went up with him said, We cannot go up against the people,—for stronger, are they than we.
texts.num.13.32: So they sent forth a rumour of the land which they had spied out, among the sons of Israel, saying,—As touching the land through which we passed to spy it out, it is, land that eateth up them who dwell therein, And all the people that we saw in the midst thereof, were men of great stature.
texts.num.13.33: And, there, saw we the giants, sons of Anak [descended] of the giants,—And we were in our own eyes, as grass-hoppers, And, so, were we in their eyes.
texts.num.14.1: Then did all the assembly lift up, and give forth their voice,—and the people wept throughout that night.
texts.num.14.2: And all the sons of Israel, murmured against Moses and against Aaron,—and all the assembly said unto them—Oh that we had died in the land of Egypt, Or in this wilderness, oh that we had died!
texts.num.14.3: Wherefore then is Yahweh bringing us into this land, to fall by the sword? Our wives and little ones, will become a prey! Would it not be well for us to go back towards Egypt?
texts.num.14.4: And they said, one to another,—Let us appoint a head and let us go back towards Egypt.
texts.num.14.5: Then did Moses and Aaron fall upon their faces,—before all the convocation of the assembly of the sons of Israel.
texts.num.14.6: But, Joshua son of Nun, and Caleb son of Jephunneh, of them who spied out the land, rent their clothes;
texts.num.14.7: and spake unto all the assembly of the sons of Israel, saying,—As for the land through which we passed to spy it out, Good, is the land, exceedingly,
texts.num.14.8: If Yahweh delight in us, then will he bring us into this land, and give it unto us,—A land which doth flow with milk and honey.
texts.num.14.9: Only against Yahweh, do not rebel. Do not, ye, fear the people of the land, For our food, they are,—Their shade hath departed, from over them. And Yahweh is with us, Do not fear them!
texts.num.14.10: But when all the assembly bade stone them with stones, the glory of Yahweh, appeared, in the tent of meeting, unto all the sons of Israel.
texts.num.14.11: Then said Yahweh unto Moses How long! must this people, despise me? And how long can they not believe in me. in view of all the signs which I have done in their midst?
texts.num.14.12: Let me smite them with pestilence, and disinherit them,—And make thee into a nation greater and more mighty than they!
texts.num.14.13: Then said Moses unto Yahweh,—So shall the Egyptians hear, For thou hast brought up. in thy might, this people out of their midst;
texts.num.14.14: And will tell it unto the inhabitants of this land: They have heard, That, thou, Yahweh, art in the midst of this people,—That eye to eye, is he seen—thou, Yahweh, And thy cloud, is standing over them, And in a pillar of cloud, thou thyself, art going on before them by day, And in a pillar of fire, by night.
texts.num.14.15: As soon, therefore, as thou hast put to death this people as one man, so soon will the nations who have heard thy fame speak saying:
texts.num.14.16: Because Yahweh, was not able, to bring in this people into the land which he had sworn unto them, therefore did he slay them in the desert.
texts.num.14.17: Now, therefore, I beseech thee let the might of My Lord, be magnified,—according as thou didst speak saying:
texts.num.14.18: Yahweh—slow to anger and great in lovingkindness, Forgiving iniquity and transgression: Though he will not leave, wholly unpunished, Visiting the iniquity of fathers upon sons, Upon a third generation, and upon a fourth.
texts.num.14.19: Pardon I beseech thee, the iniquity of this people, According to the greatness of thy lovingkindness,—And according as thou hast forgiven this people, from Egypt even thus far.
texts.num.14.20: And Yahweh said, I have pardoned according to thy word;
texts.num.14.21: Nevertheless as I live,—and that all the earth may be filled with the glory of Yahweh,
texts.num.14.22: Verily, none of the men who have been beholding my glory and my signs, which I have done in Egypt and in the desert,—and have put me to the proof these ten times, and have not hearkened unto my voice,
texts.num.14.23: shall see the land, which I sware to their fathers,—yea, none of my despisers, shall see it.
texts.num.14.24: But my servant Caleb—because there was another spirit with him, and he followed me fully, therefore will I bring him into the land whereinto he entered, and his seed, shall possess it.
texts.num.14.25: Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites, are dwelling in the valley,—to-morrow, turn ye away; and set yourselves forward towards the desert by the way of the Red Sea.
texts.num.14.26: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying:
texts.num.14.27: How long, as regardeth this evil assembly, are they to be murmuring against me? The murmuring of the sons of Israel which, they, have been murmuring against me, have I heard,
texts.num.14.28: Say unto them: As I live, is the oracle of Yahweh: Surely as ye have spoken in mine ears, so, will I do unto you:—
texts.num.14.29: In this desert, shall your dead bodies fall And none of you who were numbered in all your counting, from twenty years old and upwards,—who have murmured against me,
texts.num.14.30: none of you, shall enter into the land, as to which I uplifted my hand to give you an abode therein,—save Caleb son of Jephunneh, and Joshua, son of Nun:
texts.num.14.31: whereas, your little ones, of whom ye said, they should become, a prey, I will bring them in, and they shall acknowledge the land which ye refused.
texts.num.14.32: But, your own dead bodies, shall fall in this desert;
texts.num.14.33: and your sons, shall be shepherds in the desert forty years, and shall bear your unchastities,—until your dead bodies are consumed in the desert.
texts.num.14.34: By the number of the days wherein ye spied out the land—forty days, each day for a year, shall they bear your iniquities—forty years,—so shall ye know my opposition.
texts.num.14.35: I—Yahweh, have spoken, Verily this, will I do to all this evil assembly, who have conspired against me,—In this desert, shall they be consumed And there, shall they die.
texts.num.14.36: Now as for the men whom Moses sent to spy out the land,—who returned and caused all the assembly to murmur against him by giving out a rumour against the land,
texts.num.14.37: they died—the men who gave out an evil rumour of the land,—by the plague, before Yahweh.
texts.num.14.38: But, Joshua son of Nun, and Caleb son of Jephunneh! remained alive—of those men who went to spy out the land.
texts.num.14.39: And Moses spake these words unto all the sons of Israel, and the people were greatly depressed.
texts.num.14.40: So they arose early in the morning, and went up into the top of the mountain, saying,—We are here—therefore will we go up into the place as to which Yahweh hath said that we have sinned.
texts.num.14.41: But Moses said, Wherefore is it that, ye, are going beyond the bidding of Yahweh,—since that cannot prosper?
texts.num.14.42: Do not go up, For Yahweh is not in your midst,—Lest ye be smitten down before your enemies.
texts.num.14.43: For, the Amalekites and the Canaanites, are there before you, So shall ye fall by the sword,—For inasmuch as ye have turned back from following Yahweh, Therefore will Yahweh not be with you.
texts.num.14.44: But they presumptuously ascended into the top of the mountain,—though, neither, the ark of the covenant of Yahweh nor Moses moved out of the midst of the camp.
texts.num.14.45: So ten the Amalekites and the Canaanites, that dwelt in that mountain, came down,—and smote them and routed them even unto Hormah.
texts.num.15.1: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.15.2: Speak unto the sons of Israel, and thou shall say unto them,—When ye shall enter into the land of your dwelling-places, which, I, am giving unto you;
texts.num.15.3: and ye would offer, as an altar-flame unto Yahweh an ascending-offering or a sacrifice, for celebrating a vow or as a freewill-offering, or in your appointed seasons,—by way of offering a satisfying odour unto Yahweh, from the herd or from the flock,
texts.num.15.4: then shall he that bringeth near his oblation bring near unto Yahweh a meal-offering, of fine meal a tenth part [of an ephah] overflowed with the fourth part of a hin of oil;
texts.num.15.5: wine also for a drink-offering, the fourth part of a hin, shalt thou offer with the ascending-offering or with the sacrifice,—for each he-lamb.
texts.num.15.6: Or, with a ram, thou shalt offer a meal-offering, of fine meal, two tenths,—overflowed with oil, the third of a hin;
texts.num.15.7: wine also, for a drink-offering, the third of a hin, shalt thou bring near as a satisfying odour unto Yahweh.
texts.num.15.8: And when thou wouldest offer a choice young bullock as an ascending-offering or sacrifice,—for celebrating a vow or as a peace-offering unto Yahweh,
texts.num.15.9: then shall he bring near with his choice young bullock, a meal-offering, of fine meal three tenths,—overflowed with half a hin of oil;
texts.num.15.10: wine also, shalt thou bring near for a drink-offering, half a hin,—for an altar-flame of satisfying odour unto Yahweh.
texts.num.15.11: Thus and thus, shall it be done, for each ox, and for each ram,—and for each young one among the sheep, or among the goats:
texts.num.15.12: according to the number which ye shall offer, thus and thus, shall ye do for each one according to their number.
texts.num.15.13: Every one born in the land, thus and thus, shall offer these things,—when bringing near an altar-flame of a satisfying odour unto Yahweh.
texts.num.15.14: And when there shall sojourn with you a sojourner, or one who is in your midst to your generations, and he would offer an altar-flame of a satisfying odour unto Yahweh, as ye offer, so, shall he offer,
texts.num.15.15: In the convocation, one statute, shall there be for you and for the sojourner who sojourneth,—an age-abiding statute unto your generations, as ye are, so, the sojourner, shall be before Yahweh:
texts.num.15.16: one law and one regulation, shall there be for yourselves and for the sojourner that sojourneth with you.
texts.num.15.17: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.15.18: Speak unto the sons of Israel, and thou shalt say unto them,—When ye enter into the land whereinto I, am bringing you,
texts.num.15.19: then shall it be, when ye eat the bread of the land, that ye shall heave up a heave-offering unto Yahweh.
texts.num.15.20: Of the first of your meal, shall ye heave up, a cake, as a heave-offering,—like the heave-offering of grain, so shall ye heave it.
texts.num.15.21: Of the first of your meal, shall ye give unto Yahweh a heave-offering,—unto your generations.
texts.num.15.22: And when ye shall make a mistake, and not observe all these commandments,—which Yahweh hath spoken unto Moses;
texts.num.15.23: even all that Yahweh hath given unto you in command, by the hand of Moses,—from the day that Yahweh gave command, and onward unto your generations,
texts.num.15.24: then shall it be—if, any from the eyes of the assembly, it hath been done by mistake, that all the assembly shall offer one choice young bullock for an ascending-sacrifice as a satisfying odour unto Yahweh, with the meal-offering thereof and the drink-offering thereof, according to the regulation,—and one young he-goat as a sin-bearer.
texts.num.15.25: So shall the priest put a propitiatory, covering over all the assembly of the sons of Israel and pardon shall be granted unto them,—because a mistake, it was, they, therefore have brought in their offering—an altar-flame unto Yahweh and their sin-bearer before Yahweh for their mistake:
texts.num.15.26: and pardon shall be granted unto all the assembly of the sons of Israel and unto the sojourner that sojourneth in their midst,—for, in the case of all the people, it was, by mistake.
texts.num.15.27: And if, any one person, shall sin by mistake, then shall he bring near a she-goat of the first year as a sin-bearer;
texts.num.15.28: and the priest shall put a propitiatory-covering over the person who hath made the mistake, when he hath sinned by mistake before Yahweh, even put a propitiatory-covering over him, and pardon shall be granted him.
texts.num.15.29: For the native born among the sons of Israel, and for the sojourner that sojourneth in their midst, one law, shall there be unto you—for acting by mistake.
texts.num.15.30: But, as for the person who acteth with a high hand—of the native born or of the sojourners, Yahweh himself, he, reproacheth,—therefore shall that person be cut off out of the midst of his people.
texts.num.15.31: Because the word of Yahweh, hath he despised, and his commandment, hath he broken, that person shall be surely cut off, his iniquity, is in himself.
texts.num.15.32: While the sons of Israel were in the desert, they found a man gathering sticks on the sabbath day.
texts.num.15.33: And they who found him gathering sticks, brought him near, unto Moses and unto Aaron and unto all the assembly.
texts.num.15.34: And they put him in ward,—because it was not clear what they should do unto him.
texts.num.15.35: Then said Yahweh unto Moses, The man shall be, put to death,—all the assembly, stoning him with stones, outside the camp.
texts.num.15.36: So then all the assembly, put him forth, outside the camp, and stoned him with stones, and he died,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.num.15.37: And Yahweh spake unto Moses saying:
texts.num.15.38: Speak unto the sons of Israel, and thou shalt say unto them, That they shall make them fringes on the corners of their garments unto their generations—and shall put upon the fringe of the corner a cord of blue:
texts.num.15.39: so shall they serve you as fringes, and when ye see then, then shall ye call to mind all the commandments of Yahweh, and shall do them,—and shall not spy out, after your own hearts, and after your own eyes for things, after which, ye, are ready to go unchastely away:
texts.num.15.40: to the intent ye may call to mind, and do all my commandments, and be holy unto your God.
texts.num.15.41: I—Yahweh, am your God—who brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, to become your God,—I,—Yahweh, am your God.
texts.num.16.1: Then took Korah, son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi,—and Dathan and Abiram sons of Eliab, and On, son of Peleth sons of Reuben;
texts.num.16.2: and rose up before Moses, with certain men of the sons of Israel, two hundred and fifty,—princes of assembly, called to the stated meeting, men of renown;
texts.num.16.3: and gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron and said unto them Too much for you, when, all the assembly, are, all of them, holy, and in the midst of them, is Yahweh,—Wherefore, then, should ye set yourselves up, above the convocation of Yahweh?
texts.num.16.4: And, when Moses heard it, he fell upon his face.
texts.num.16.5: Then spake he unto Korah, and unto all his assembly, saying, In the morning, will Yahweh make known who are his, and who is the holy one and will cause him to come near unto himself,—yea him whom he shall choose, will he cause to come near unto himself.
texts.num.16.6: This do,—Take to you censers, Korah and all his assembly;
texts.num.16.7: and place therein fire, and put thereon incense before Yahweh, to-morrow, So shall it be—that, the man whom Yahweh shall choose, he shall be the holy one. Too much for you ye sons of Levi!
texts.num.16.8: And Moses said unto Korah,—Hear, I pray you, ye sons of Levi!
texts.num.16.9: Is it too small a thing for you that the God of Israel hath separated you from the assembly of Israel, to bring you near unto himself,—to do the laborious work of the habitation of Yahweh, and to stand before the assembly, to wait upon them?
texts.num.16.10: But having brought thee near, and all thy brethren the sons of Levi with thee, must ye seek priesthood also?
texts.num.16.11: Wherefore thou and all thine assembly, are conspiring against Yahweh,—But Aaron, what is he, that ye should murmur against him?
texts.num.16.12: Then sent Moses, to call for Dathan and for Abiram sons of Eliab,—and they said We will not come up:
texts.num.16.13: Was it, a small thing, that thou didst bring us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to put us to death in the desert but thou must, continue even to lord it, over us?
texts.num.16.14: Certainly not into a land flowing with milk and honey, hast thou brought us, nor given unto us an inheritance of field and vineyard,—The eyes of those men, wilt thou dig out? We will not come up.
texts.num.16.15: Then was Moses very angry, and he said unto Yahweh, Do not thou have respect unto their meal-offering. Not one ass, from them, have I taken, neither have I wronged one of them.
texts.num.16.16: And Moses said unto Korah, Thou, and all thine assembly, come ye before Yahweh,—thou, and they, and Aaron to-morrow.
texts.num.16.17: And take ye each man his censer and put thereon incense, then shall ye bring near before Yahweh, each man his censer, two hundred and fifty Censers,—and, thou and Aaron, each man his censer.
texts.num.16.18: So they took each man his censer and put thereon fire, and placed thereon incense,—and took their stand at the entrance of the tent of meeting with Moses and Aaron.
texts.num.16.19: And Korah gathered together against them all the assembly, unto the entrance of the tent of meeting,—then appeared the glory of Yahweh, unto all the assembly.
texts.num.16.20: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying:
texts.num.16.21: Separate yourselves out of the midst of this assembly,—that I may consume them in a moment.
texts.num.16.22: And they fell upon their faces and said, O GOD, the God of the spirits of all flesh,—shall, one man, sin, and against all the assembly, wilt thou be wroth.
texts.num.16.23: And Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying,
texts.num.16.24: Speak unto the assembly, saying,—Get ye up from round about the habitation of Korah, Dathan and Abiram.
texts.num.16.25: So Moses rose up, and went, unto Dathan and Abiram,—then went, after him the elders of Israel.
texts.num.16.26: And he spake unto the assembly, saying—Remove I pray you from beside the tents of these lawless men, and do not touch aught that pertaineth unto them,—lest ye be carried off, in all their sins.
texts.num.16.27: So they went up from beside the habitation of Korah, Dathan and Abiram on every side,—and, Dathan and Abiram, came out and stationed themselves at the entrance of their tents, with their wives and their sons and their little ones.
texts.num.16.28: Then said Moses, Hereby, shall ye know, that, Yahweh hath sent me, to do all these works,—verily, not out of my own heart:
texts.num.16.29: If, as all human beings die, these do die, and the visitation of all human beings, be visited upon them, Yahweh, hath not sent me.
texts.num.16.30: But, if, a creation, Yahweh create, and the ground open wide her mouth and swallow them up, with all that pertain unto them, and so they go down alive unto hades, then shall ye know, that these men have despised Yahweh.
texts.num.16.31: And it came to pass as he made an end of speaking all these words, that the ground which was under them, clave asunder;
texts.num.16.32: and the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed up them, and their households,—and all the human beings who pertained unto Korah, with all their goods:
texts.num.16.33: so, they, and all that pertained unto them, went down, alive unto hades,—and the earth, closed upon them, and they perished out of the midst of the convocation.
texts.num.16.34: And, all Israel who were round about them, fled at their cry,—for they said, Lest the earth swallow us up.
texts.num.16.35: Fire also came forth, from Yahweh,—and consumed the two hundred and fifty men, who offered the incense.
texts.num.16.36: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.16.37: Say unto Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, that he take up the censers out of the midst of the burning, and the fire, scatter thou yonder,—for they have been hallowed.
texts.num.16.38: As for the censers of these sinners against their own persons, they shall be made into beaten-out plates as an overlay for the altar, for they had brought them near before Yahweh and hallowed them,—so shall they become a sign unto the sons of Israel.
texts.num.16.39: And Eleazar the priest took the censers of bronze, which the consumed men had brought near,—and beat them out into plates for overlaying the altar:
texts.num.16.40: a memorial unto the sons of Israel, That no stranger, who is not of the seed of Aaron, shall draw near to offer incense before Yahweh,—lest he become like Korah and like his assembly, As spake Yahweh by the hand of Moses with regard thereto.
texts.num.16.41: And all the assembly of the sons of Israel murmured, on the morrow, against Moses and against, Aaron, saying,—Ye, have caused the death of the people of Yahweh.
texts.num.16.42: And it came to pass, when the assembly gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, that they turned towards the tent of meeting, and lo! the cloud had covered it: and the glory of Yahweh, appeared.
texts.num.16.43: And Moses and Aaron came in, before the tent of meeting.
texts.num.16.44: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.16.45: Lift yourselves up out of the midst of this assembly, that I may consume them, as in a moment,—And they fell upon their faces.
texts.num.16.46: Then said Moses unto Aaron—Take the censer and place thereon fire, from off the altar, and put incense [thereon], and, going quickly into the assembly, put a propitiatory-covering over them,—for wrath hath gone forth from before Yahweh the plague, hath begun.
texts.num.16.47: Then took Aaron, as Moses spake, and ran into the midst of the convocation, and lo! the plague had begun among the people,—so he placed the incense, and put a propitiatory-covering over the people:
texts.num.16.48: thus did he take his stand between the dead and the living,—and the plague was restrained.
texts.num.16.49: And so it was that they who died in the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred,—besides them who died over the matter of Korah.
texts.num.16.50: And Aaron returned unto Moses, unto the entrance of the tent of meeting,—when, the plague, had been restrained.
texts.num.17.1: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.17.2: Speak unto the sons of Israel and take of them one staff each for an ancestral house of all their princes, by their ancestral houses, twelve staves,—each man’s name, shalt thou write upon his staff;
texts.num.17.3: and, Aaron’s name, shalt thou write upon the staff of Levi,—for, one staff, shall there be for the head of their ancestral house.
texts.num.17.4: Then shalt thou lay them up in the tent of meeting,—before the testimony, where I meet with you.
texts.num.17.5: So shall it come to pass, that, the man whom I shall choose, his staff, shall bud,—so will I cause to cease from against me the murmurings of the sons of Israel, wherewith they, are murmuring against you.
texts.num.17.6: And Moses spake unto the sons of Israel and every one of their princes gave unto him, a staff apiece, for each prince, by their ancestral houses, twelve staves,—and the staff of Aaron, was in the midst of their staves.
texts.num.17.7: So Moses laid up the staves before Yahweh,—in the tent of the testimony.
texts.num.17.8: And it came to pass, on the morrow, that Moses entered into the tent of the testimony; and lo! the staff of Aaron for the house of Levi, had budded,—yea it had brought forth buds and bloomed blossoms, and borne ripe almonds.
texts.num.17.9: So then Moses brought forth all the staves, from before Yahweh, unto all the sons of Israel,—and they saw and took, each man his own staff.
texts.num.17.10: And Yahweh said unto Moses—Put back the rod of Aaron, before the testimony, to be kept as a sign unto such as are perverse,—that thou mayest bring to an end their murmurings against me that they die not.
texts.num.17.11: Thus did Moses,—as Yahweh commanded him, so, did he.
texts.num.17.12: Then spake the sons of Israel unto Moses saying: Lo! we have breathed our last—we are lost, we are, all, lost:
texts.num.17.13: whosoever draweth near—draweth near—unto the habitation of Yahweh, dieth,—are we ever to have made an end of breathing our last?
texts.num.18.1: And Yahweh said unto Aaron, Thou and thy sons and the house of thy father with thee, shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary,—and, thou, and thy sons with thee, shall bear the iniquity of your priesthood.
