texts.num.18.2: Therefore also thy brethren of the tribe of Levi the stem of thy father, bring thou near with thee, and let them be joined unto thee, and let them wait upon thee,—both on thee and on thy sons with thee, before the tent of the testimony.
texts.num.18.3: So shall they keep thy charge, and the charge of all the tent,—only, unto the vessels of the sanctuary, and unto the altar, shall they not come near, lest they die—both they, and ye.
texts.num.18.4: So shall they be joined unto thee, and shall keep the charge of the tent of meeting, as to all the laborious work of the tent,—but a stranger, shall not come near unto you.
texts.num.18.5: So shall ye keep the charge of the sanctuary, and the charge of the altar,—that there no more be wrath against the sons of Israel.
texts.num.18.6: I, therefore, lo! I have taken your brethren the Levites, out of the midst of the sons of Israel,—unto you, as a gift are they given, unto Yahweh, to do the laborious work of the tent of meeting.
texts.num.18.7: But thou and thy sons with thee, shall keep the charge of your priesthood, as to every matter of the altar and as to the interior of the veil, and shall do the laborious work, as a laborious service of gifts, do I give your priesthood, and, the stranger who cometh near shall be put to death.
texts.num.18.8: And Yahweh spake unto Aaron, I, therefore, lo! I have given unto thee the charge of my heave-offerings,—as to all the hallowed things of the sons of Israel—unto thee, have I given them. as pertaining to the anointing, and unto thy sons. for a statute age-abiding,
texts.num.18.9: This, shall be thine, out of the things most holy, out of the fire,—their every oblation—to the extent of their every meal-offering, and their every sin-bearer, and their every guilt-bearer wherewith they make amends unto me, most holy unto thee, shall it be and unto thy sons.
texts.num.18.10: As something most holy, shall ye eat it,—every male, shall eat it, holy, shall it be unto thee.
texts.num.18.11: This, therefore, shall be thine—the heave-offering of their gift even all the wave-offerings of the sons of Israel, unto thee, have I given them and unto thy sons and unto thy daughters with thee by a statute age-abiding,—every one that is clean in thy house, shall eat it.
texts.num.18.12: All the best of oil, and all the best of new-wine and corn,—the firstfruits thereof which they shall give unto Yahweh, unto thee, have I given them.
texts.num.18.13: The firstfruits of all that is in their land which they shall bring in unto Yahweh, thine, shall it be,—every one that is clean in thy house, shall eat it:
texts.num.18.14: every devoted thing in Israel, thine, shall it be:
texts.num.18.15: every thing that is born first of all flesh that may be offered unto Yahweh among men and among beasts, shall be thine,—only thou shalt, redeem, the firstborn of men, and the firstborn of unclean beasts, shalt thou redeem.
texts.num.18.16: And, as to the redemption price thereof, from a month old, shalt thou redeem, by thine estimate five shekels of silver by the shekel of the sanctuary,—twenty gerahs, it is.
texts.num.18.17: Only a firstling ox or a firstling sheep or a firstling goat, shalt thou not redeem, hallowed, they are,—their blood, shalt thou dash against the altar and of their fat, shalt thou make a perfume, an altar-flame, for a satisfying odour unto Yahweh:
texts.num.18.18: and their flesh, shall be thine,—as the wave-breast and as the right leg, thine, shall it be:
texts.num.18.19: all the heave-offerings of the holy things which the sons of Israel shall heave up unto Yahweh, have I given unto thee and unto thy sons and unto thy daughters with thee by a statute age-abiding,—an age-abiding covenant of salt, it is before Yahweh, for thee and for thy seed with thee.
texts.num.18.20: Then said Yahweh unto Aaron: In their land, thou shalt have no inheritance, and no allotted portion, shalt thou have in their midst,—I, am thine allotted portion and thine inheritance in the midst of the sons of Israel.
texts.num.18.21: And unto the sons of Levi, lo! I have given all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance,—the allotted portion for their laborious work which, they are performing, the laborious work of the tent of meeting:
texts.num.18.22: that the sons of Israel come near no more, unto the tent of meeting,—to bear sin, to die.
texts.num.18.23: So shall the Levites themselves perform the laborious work of the tent of meeting, and, they, shall bear their iniquity, a statute age-abiding, unto your generations, and in the midst of the sons of Israel, shall they take no inheritance.
texts.num.18.24: Because the tenth of the sons of Israel which they shall offer up unto Yahweh as a heave-offering, have I given unto the Levites as an inheritance,—for this cause, said I regarding them, In the midst of the sons of Israel, shall they take no inheritance.
texts.num.18.25: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.18.26: Unto the Levites, therefore shalt thou speak and shalt say unto them, When ye shall take of the sons of Israel the tenth which I have given unto you from them as your inheritance, then shall ye offer up therefrom the heave-offering of Yahweh, a tenth of the tenth.
texts.num.18.27: So shall your heave-offering be reckoned your own,—as corn out of the threshing-floor, and as the abundance out of the wine-press.
texts.num.18.28: Thus, shall ye also, offer up the heave-offering of Yahweh, out of all your tenths which ye shall take from the sons of Israel,—and give therefrom the heave-offering of Yahweh, unto Aaron the priest.
texts.num.18.29: Out of all your gifts, shall ye offer up every heave-offering of Yahweh,—out of all the best thereof, the hallowed pert thereof out of it.
texts.num.18.30: And thou shalt say unto them,—When ye offer the best thereof out of it, then shall it be reckoned to belong unto the Levites, as the increase of the threshing-floor and as the increase of the wine-press,
texts.num.18.31: And ye shall eat it in any place, ye, and your household,—for a reward, it is unto you, the allotted portion for your laborious work in the tent of meeting.
texts.num.18.32: And ye shall not by reason of it bear sin, when ye offer up the best thereof, out of it; and the hallowed things of the sons of Israel, shall ye not profane neither shall ye die.
texts.num.19.1: And Yahweh spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying:
texts.num.19.2: This, is the statute of the law, which Yahweh hath commanded, saying,—Speak unto the sons of Israel—That they bring unto thee a red heifer, without defect wherein is no blemish, and whereupon hath come no yoke.
texts.num.19.3: Then shall ye give her unto Eleazar the priest, and he shall take her forth unto the outside of the camp, and she shall be slain before him;
texts.num.19.4: and Eleazar the priest shall take of her blood with his finger,—and shall sprinkle towards the front of the tent of meeting: of her blood, seven times;
texts.num.19.5: and the heifer shall be burned up before his eyes,—her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, with her dung shall be burned up.
texts.num.19.6: Then shall the priest take cedar-wood and hyssop and crimson,—and cast into the midst of the burning up of the heifer.
texts.num.19.7: And the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his flesh in water, and afterwards come into the camp,—but the priest shall be unclean until the evening,
texts.num.19.8: And, he that burneth her, shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water,—and be unclean until the evening,
texts.num.19.9: Then shall a man that is clean gather up the ashes of the heifer, and put them by, outside the camp, in a clean place,—so shall they be for the assembly of the sons of Israel to keep for water of separation it is a taking away of sin.
texts.num.19.10: Then shall he that gathered up the ashes wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening,—so shall it be for the sons of Israel and for the sojourner that sojourneth in your midst by a statute age-abiding.
texts.num.19.11: He that toucheth the dead, even any human person, shall be unclean seven days.
texts.num.19.12: He, shall cleanse himself from sin therewith on the third day, then on the seventh day, shall he be clean,—but if he cleanse not himself from sin on the third day, then on the seventh day, shall he not be clean,
texts.num.19.13: Whosoever toucheth the dead the person of the human being that dieth and doth not cleanse himself from sin, the habitation of Yahweh, hath he made unclean; that person therefore shall be cut off out of Israel,—because, the water of separation, was not dashed upon him, unclean, shall he be, his uncleanness is yet upon him.
texts.num.19.14: This, is the law—When, a human being, shall die in a tent, every one who goeth into the tent and every one who is in the tent shall be unclean seven days.
texts.num.19.15: And, in the case of every open vessel, on which no cover is fastened, unclean, it is.
texts.num.19.16: And, whosoever toucheth on the face of the field, one slain with a sword, or one who hath died, or a human bone or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.
texts.num.19.17: And they shall take, for him that is unclean, of the ashes of the burning of the sin-bearer,—and living water shall be put thereon in a vessel,
texts.num.19.18: Then shall a man that is clean take hyssop, and dip in the water, and sprinkle upon the tent, and upon all the vessels, and upon the persons who were there,—and upon him that touched the bone or him who had been slain, or him who had died of himself or the grave;
texts.num.19.19: and the clean person shall sprinkle upon the unclean, on the third day, and on the seventh day,—so shall he cleanse himself from sin, on the seventh day, and shall wash his clothes, and bathe in water and be clean in the evening.
texts.num.19.20: But in the case of the man who shall be unclean and shall not cleanse himself from sin, that person shall be cut off, out of the midst of the convocation,—for, the sanctuary of Yahweh, hath he made unclean, the water of separation, hath not been dashed upon him unclean, he is.
texts.num.19.21: So shall it be unto them for statute age-abiding,—and, he that sprinkleth the water of separation, shall wash his clothes, and he that toucheth the water of separation shall be unclean until the evening;
texts.num.19.22: and, whatsoever the unclean person toucheth, shall be unclean,—and the person who toucheth it shall be unclean until the evening.
texts.num.20.1: Then came the sons of Israel the whole assembly, into the desert of Zin in the first month, and the people dwelt in Kadesh,—and Miriam died there, and was buried there.
texts.num.20.2: And there was no water for the assembly,—so they gathered together against Moses and against Aaron.
texts.num.20.3: And the people contended with Moses,—and spake saying, Would then we had died when our brethren died, before Yahweh!
texts.num.20.4: Wherefore then hast thou brought the convocation of Yahweh into this desert,—to die there, we, and our cattle?
texts.num.20.5: And wherefore did ye cause us to come up out of Egypt, to bring us into this wretched place?—not a place of seeds, and figs, and vines and pomegranates, even water, is there none to drink.
texts.num.20.6: And Moses and Aaron went in from the presence of the multitude unto the entrance of the tent of meeting, and fell upon their faces,—and the glory of Yahweh appeared unto them.
texts.num.20.7: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.20.8: Take the staff and gather together the assembly, thou, and Aaron thy brother, then shall ye speak unto the cliff before their eyes and it shall give forth its waters,—so shalt thou bring forth unto them water, out of the cliff, and shalt cause the assembly, and their cattle to drink.
texts.num.20.9: And Moses took the staff from before Yahweh,—as he commanded him.
texts.num.20.10: And Moses and Aaron gathered together the convocation before the cliff,—and he said unto them: Hear I pray you ye rebels! Out of this cliff, must we bring forth for you water?
texts.num.20.11: And Moses lifted high his hand and smote the cliff with his staff, twice,—and there came forth water in abundance, and the assembly and their cattle, did drink.
texts.num.20.12: Then said Yahweh unto Moses and unto Aaron, Because ye believed not in me, to hallow me in the eyes of the sons of Israel, therefore, shall ye not bring in this convocation into the land which I have given unto them.
texts.num.20.13: The same, were the waters of Meribah [that is "Contention"] in that the sons of Israel contended with Yahweh,—and so he hallowed himself among them.
texts.num.20.14: And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh, unto the king of Edom,—Thus, saith thy brother Israel, Thou thyself, knowest all the distress which befell us;
texts.num.20.15: and how our fathers went down to Egypt, and we abode in Egypt, many days, and that the Egyptians ill-treated us, and our fathers;
texts.num.20.16: and we made outcry unto Yahweh, and he heard our voice, and sent a messenger, and brought us forth out of Egypt,—lo! then, we, are in Kadesh, a city at the extremity of thy boundary,
texts.num.20.17: Let us, we pray thee, pass through thy land—we will not pass through field or vineyard, nor will we drink the waters of a well,—by the king’s road, will we go—we will turn neither to the right hand nor to the left, until we get through thy boundary.
texts.num.20.18: And Edom said unto him, Thou shalt not pass through my land,—lest with the sword, I come out to meet thee.
texts.num.20.19: And the sons of Israel said unto him—By the highway, will we go up, and if thy waters, we should drink—I, and my cattle then would I give the price thereof,—only—it is nothing!—with my feet, would I pass through.
texts.num.20.20: And he said, Thou shalt not pass through. And Edom came out to meet him, with a strong people, and with a firm hand.
texts.num.20.21: Thus did Edom refuse to give Israel passage through his boundary,—and Israel turned away from him.
texts.num.20.22: Then set they forward from Kadesh,—and the sons of Israel. all the assembly, came in to Mount Hor.
texts.num.20.23: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses and unto Aaron in Mount Hor,—near the boundary of the land of Edom saying:
texts.num.20.24: Aaron shall be withdrawn unto his kinsfolk, for he shall not enter into the land. which I have given unto the sons of Israel,—because ye spurned my bidding, at the waters of Meribah.
texts.num.20.25: Take thou Aaron, and Eleazar his son,—and bring them up Mount Hor;
texts.num.20.26: and strip thou Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son,—and, Aaron, shall be withdrawn and shall die there.
texts.num.20.27: And Moses did as Yahweh commanded,—and they went up into, Mount Hor, in sight of all the assembly.
texts.num.20.28: And Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them upon Eleazar his son, and Aaron died there, in the top of the mount,—and Moses and Eleazar came down out of the mount.
texts.num.20.29: And all the assembly saw that Aaron was dead; and they bewailed Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.
texts.num.21.1: And the Canaanite, the king of Arad who dwelt in the South, heard that Israel had entered by the way of Atharim,—so he made war with Israel, and took some of them captive.
texts.num.21.2: Then Israel vowed vow unto Yahweh, and said,—If thou wilt, surely deliver up, this people into my hand, then will I utterly destroy their cities.
texts.num.21.3: And Yahweh hearkened unto the voice of Israel and delivered up the Canaanite into his hand, so he utterly destroyed them, and their cities, and called the name of the place Hormah [that is, "Utter Destruction"].
texts.num.21.4: Then brake they up from Mount Hor, by way of the Red Sea, to go round the land of Edom,—and the soul of the people became impatient because of the way,
texts.num.21.5: So then the people spake against God and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt, to die in the desert? for there is neither bread nor water, and our soul, doth loathe this contemptible bread!
texts.num.21.6: And Yahweh sent among the people the poisonous serpents, and they bit the people,—and much people out of Israel died.
texts.num.21.7: Then came the people of Israel unto Moses and said—We have sinned in that we spake against Yahweh and against thee, Pray thou unto Yahweh, that he may take from us the serpent. So Moses prayed for the people.
texts.num.21.8: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Make thee a like serpent, and put it upon standard,—and it shall come to pass, that, any one who is bitten, as soon as he seeth it, shall live.
texts.num.21.9: So Moses made a serpent of bronze, and put it upon the standard,—and it came to pass—that if the serpent had bitten any man, as soon as he directed his look unto the serpent of bronze, he lived.
texts.num.21.10: And the sons of Israel brake up,—and encamped in Oboth.
texts.num.21.11: And they brake up from Oboth,—and encamped in Ije-Abarim, in the desert which is over against Moab, towards the rising of the sun.
texts.num.21.12: From thence, brake they up,—and encamped in the ravine of Zered.
texts.num.21.13: From thence, brake they up, and encamped on the other side of Arnon which is in the desert, that cometh forth out of the boundary of the Amorites,—for, Arnon, is the boundary of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
texts.num.21.14: For this cause is it said, in the Book of the Wars of Yahweh,— …Waheb with a hurricane, And the ravines of Arnon;
texts.num.21.15: And the bottom of the ravines, that extendeth toward the dwelling of Ar,—And adjoineth to the boundary of Moab,
texts.num.21.16: And from thence, towards Beer,—the same, is the well whereof Yahweh said unto Moses, Gather together the people, that I may give them water.
texts.num.21.17: Then, sang Israel this song,—Spring thou up, O well! Respond ye thereunto;
texts.num.21.18: A well!—princes digged it, Nobles of the people, delved it, With a sceptre, With their staves. And, from the desert, to Mattanah;
texts.num.21.19: and from Mattanah, to Nahaliel; and from Nahaliel, to Bamoth;
texts.num.21.20: and, from Bamoth of the valley, which is in the field-country of Moab, to the top of Pisgah,—which overlooketh Jeshimon.
texts.num.21.21: Then sent Israel messengers, unto Sihon king of the Amorites, saying:
texts.num.21.22: Let me pass through thy land we will not turn aside into field or into vineyard, nor will we drink the water of a well,—by the king’s road, will we go, until we get through thy boundary.
texts.num.21.23: And Sihon suffered not Israel to pass through his boundary, but Sihon gathered together all his people, and came forth to meet Israel, towards the desert, and entered Jahaz, and fought with Israel.
texts.num.21.24: And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword,—and took possession of his land, from Arnon unto Jabbok, unto the sons of Ammon, for strong, was the boundary of the sons of Ammon.
texts.num.21.25: So Israel took all these cities,—and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and in all her villages;
texts.num.21.26: for, as for Heshbon, the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, it was, he, having fought with the former king of Moab, and taken all his land out of his hand, unto Arnon.
texts.num.21.27: For this cause, say the poets—Enter ye Heshbon,—Built and prepared be the city of Sihon;
texts.num.21.28: For, a fire, hath come forth out of Heshbon, A flame, out of the stronghold of Sihon; It hath consumed Ar of Moab, The lords of the high places of Arnon.
texts.num.21.29: Woe to thee, Moab, Thou art lost, O people of Chemosh,—He hath given up his sons as fugitives, And his daughters into captivity, Unto the king of the Amorites, Sihon.
texts.num.21.30: Then we shot them—Heshbon is destroyed, as far as Dibon,—Then laid we waste as far as Nophah, A fire reacheth unto Medeba.
texts.num.21.31: So then Israel dwelt in the land of the Amorites.
texts.num.21.32: And Moses sent to spy out Jazer, and they captured the villages thereof,—and dispossessed the Amorites that were there.
texts.num.21.33: Then turned they, and went up by the way of Bashan,—and Og, king of Bashan, came forth to meet them—he and all his people, to give battle at Edrei.
texts.num.21.34: Then said Yahweh unto Moses—Do not fear him, for into thy hand, have I delivered him and all his people, and his land,—Therefore shalt thou do unto him, as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, who was dwelling in Heshbon.
texts.num.21.35: So then they smote him and his sons and all his people, until there was not left him a remnant,—and took possession of his land.
texts.num.22.1: Then did the sons of Israel break up,—and encamp in the waste plains of Moab, on the other side of the Jordan by Jericho.
texts.num.22.2: And Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done unto the Amorites;
texts.num.22.3: and Moab shrank with great fear from the presence of the people because, many, they were,—and Moab was alarmed at the presence of the sons of Israel.
texts.num.22.4: So Moab said unto the elders of Midian—Now, shall the gathered host lick up all that are round about us, as the ox doth lick up the verdure of the field. But, Balak son of Zippor, was king unto Moab at that time.
texts.num.22.5: So he sent messengers unto Balaam son of Beor, to Pethor which was by the river of the land of the sons of his people to call him,—saying Lo! a people, hath come forth out of Egypt Lo! he hath covered the eye of the land, Yea he, is tarrying over against me.
texts.num.22.6: Now, therefore, do come, I pray thee curse me this people. For stronger, he is than I, If peradventure I prevail, we shall smite him, That I may drive him out of the land,—For I know that, he whom thou dost bless, is to be blessed, And, he whom thou dost curse, is to be cursed.
texts.num.22.7: And the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went their way, with the rewards of divination in their hand,—so they came in unto Balaam, and spake unto him the words of Balak.
texts.num.22.8: And he said unto them—Tarry ye here for the night, and I will bring you back word, as Yahweh shall speak unto me. So the princes of Moab abode with Balaam.
texts.num.22.9: And God came in unto Balaam,—and said, Who are these men with thee?
texts.num.22.10: Then said Balaam unto God,—Balak, son of Zippor king of Moab, hath sent unto me:
texts.num.22.11: Lo! the people that hath come forth out of Egypt—he covereth the eye of the land. Now, do come, do revile me him, Peradventure I shall prevail in making war with him, And shall drive him out.
texts.num.22.12: And God said unto Balaam, Thou shalt not go with them,—Thou shalt not curse the people, For blessed, he is.
texts.num.22.13: And Balaam rose up in the morning, and said unto the princes of Balak, Get you into your own land,—For Yahweh hath refused to let me go with you.
texts.num.22.14: So the princes of Moab arose, and came in unto Balak,—and said, Balaam refused to come with us.
texts.num.22.15: Then added Balak again,—to send princes, more and weightier than these.
texts.num.22.16: And they came in unto Balaam,—and said unto him—Thus, said Balak son of Zippor, Do not be withheld, I pray thee from coming unto me:
texts.num.22.17: For I will honour, thee, exceedingly, and all that thou shalt say unto me, will I do. Do come therefore I pray thee oh revile me this people.
texts.num.22.18: And Balaam responded and said unto the servants of Balak, Though Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the bidding of Yahweh my God, to do less or more.
texts.num.22.19: Now, therefore abide here, I pray you even ye,—for the night,—that I may get to know what further Yahweh may be speaking with me.
texts.num.22.20: And God came in unto Balaam, by night, and said unto him—If, to call thee, the men have come in, arise go with them,—But only, the thing that I shall speak unto thee, that, shalt thou do.
texts.num.22.21: So Balaam arose in the morning, and saddled his ass,—and went with the princes of Moab.
texts.num.22.22: Then kindled the anger of God, because he was going, and the messenger of Yahweh stationed himself in the way, to withstand him,—as he was riding upon his ass, his two young men being with him.
texts.num.22.23: And the ass saw the messenger of Yahweh stationed in the road with his drawn sword in his hand, so the ass turned aside out of the road and went into the field,—and Balaam smote the ass, to make her turn back into the road.
texts.num.22.24: But the messenger of Yahweh took his stand, in a hollow pass of the vineyards,—with a fence on this side, and a fence on that side.
texts.num.22.25: And when the ass saw the messenger of Yahweh, she squeezed herself against the wall, and squeezed the foot of Balaam against the wall,—and again he smote her.
texts.num.22.26: And the messenger of Yahweh went on further, and took his stand in a narrow place, where there was no way to turn to the right hand or to the left.
texts.num.22.27: And, when the ass saw the messenger of Yahweh, she sank down under Balaam,—then was Balaam’s anger kindled, and he smote the ass with the staff.
texts.num.22.28: And Yahweh opened the mouth of the ass,—and she said unto Balaam—What have I done to thee, that thou hast smitten me, these three times?
texts.num.22.29: And Balaam said unto the ass, Surely thou hast been making sport of me,—Would there had been a sword in my hand, for, now, would I have slain thee.
texts.num.22.30: Then said the ass unto Balaam—Am not I thine own ass on which thou hast ridden all thy life, until this day? Have I, been wont, to do unto thee, thus? And he said, Nay!
texts.num.22.31: Then did Yahweh unveil the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the messenger of Yahweh stationed in the road, with his sword drawn in his hand,—so he bent his head and bowed down before him.
texts.num.22.32: And the messenger of Yahweh said unto him, Wherefore hast thou smitten thine ass, these three times? Lo! I, myself, am come forth to withstand thee, because headlong was thy way before me.
texts.num.22.33: And the ass hath seen me, and hath turned aside at my presence these three times: Unless she had turned aside from my presence, yea now even thee, had I slain, but, her, had I suffered to live.
texts.num.22.34: Then said Balaam unto the messenger of Yahweh—I have sinned, for I knew not, that, thou, wast stationed to meet me in the road,—Now, therefore, if it be displeasing in thine eyes, I must get me back again.
texts.num.22.35: And the messenger of Yahweh said unto Balaam—Go with the men: Only the word that I shall speak unto thee, that, shalt thou speak. So Balaam went his way with the princes of Balak.
texts.num.22.36: And Balak heard that Balaam, was coming,—so he went forth to meet him unto a city of Moab which was upon the boundary of Arnon, which was in the utmost part of the boundary.
texts.num.22.37: And Balak said unto Balaam: Did I not, send, unto thee, to call thee? Wherefore didst thou not come unto me? Am I not in very deed, able to honour thee?
texts.num.22.38: And Balaam said unto Balak—Lo! I am come unto thee, Now, can, I, possibly, promise anything? The word that God shall put in my mouth, that, must I speak.
texts.num.22.39: So Balaam went with Balak,—and they entered Kiriath-huzoth.
texts.num.22.40: And Balak sacrificed herd and flock,—and sent unto Balaam, and unto the princes that were with him.
texts.num.22.41: And it came to pass in the morning, that Balak took Balaam, and brought him up the high places of Baal,—and he saw from thence the utmost part of the people.
texts.num.23.1: Then said Balaam unto Balak: Build me here seven altars,—and prepare me here, seven bullocks and seven rams.
texts.num.23.2: And Balak did as Balaam had spoken,—and Balak and Balaam caused to ascend a bullock and a ram on each altar.
texts.num.23.3: Then said Balaam unto Balak: Station thyself by thine ascending-sacrifice, and let me go my way—peradventure Yahweh may come and meet me, and what thing soever he may show me, I will tell thee. So he went his way to a bare height.
texts.num.23.4: And God came unto Balaam,—so he said unto him The seven altars, have I built in a row, and have caused to ascend, bullock and a ram on each altar.
texts.num.23.5: And Yahweh put a word into the mouth of Balaam,—and said—Return unto Balak, and, thus, shalt thou speak.
texts.num.23.6: So he returned unto him, and lo! he was stationed by his ascending-sacrifice,—he, and all the princes of Moab.
texts.num.23.7: So he took up his parable and said,—From Aram, doth Balak conduct me, The king of Moab, from the mountains of the East, Come thou! curse me Jacob, Yea, come thou! rage on Israel.
texts.num.23.8: How can I revile one whom GOD hath not reviled? Yea, how can I rage on one on whom Yahweh hath not raged?
texts.num.23.9: Surely from the head of the rocks, do I see him, Yea, from the hills, do I observe him,—Lo! a people, who alone doth dwell, And among the nations, he doth not reckon himself.
texts.num.23.10: Who hath counted the dust of Jacob? Or who hath numbered the fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the upright, And let my hereafter be like his!
texts.num.23.11: Then said Balak unto Balaam, What hast thou done for me? To revile mine enemies, I summoned thee, and lo! thou hast kept on blessing.
texts.num.23.12: And he answered and said,—Was it not to be so that whatsoever Yahweh should put into my mouth, the same, should I take heed to speak?
texts.num.23.13: Then said Balak unto him—Come, I pray thee, with me unto another place, from whence thou mayest see him, nothing but his utmost part, shalt thou see, but all of him, shalt thou not see,—and so revile me him from thence.
texts.num.23.14: And he took him to the field of Zophim, unto the head of Pisgah,—and built seven altars, and caused to ascend a bullock and a ram on each altar.
texts.num.23.15: Then said he to Balak, Station thyself here by thine ascending-sacrifice,—while, I, meet him yonder.
texts.num.23.16: And Yahweh met Balaam, and put a word into his mouth,—and said—Return unto Balak and thus shalt thou speak.
texts.num.23.17: So he came in unto him and, there he was-stationed by his ascending-sacrifice, and the princes of Moab with him. And Balak said unto him, What hath Yahweh spoken?
texts.num.23.18: Then took he up his parable and said,—Rise, Balak, and hear, Give ear unto me son of Zippor!
texts.num.23.19: GOD is, not a man, that he should lie, Nor a son of Adam, that he should repent,—Hath, he, said, and will not perform? Yea spoken, and will not make it stand fast?
texts.num.23.20: Lo! to bless, have I received [command],—And I will bless, nor will I take it back.
texts.num.23.21: He hath not discovered trouble in Jacob, Neither hath he seen wretchedness in Israel,—Yahweh, his God, is with him, And, the acclaim of a king, in his midst:
texts.num.23.22: GOD having brought them forth out of Egypt, The very horns of the buffalo, are his:
texts.num.23.23: Surely, there is no enchantment against Jacob, Nor divination against Israel,—Now, shall it be said—Of Jacob and of Israel, What hath GOD wrought!
texts.num.23.24: Lo, a people, like a lioness, shall rise, And like a strong lion, shall rouse himself up; He will not lie down till he eat the torn, And the blood of the slain, he drink.
texts.num.23.25: Then said Balak unto Balaam, Thou shalt neither revile, him,—nor bless him.
texts.num.23.26: And Balaam responded, and said unto Balak,—Spake I not unto thee, saying, All that Yahweh shall speak, that, must I do?
texts.num.23.27: And Balak said unto Balaam, Come, I pray thee! let me take thee unto another place,—peradventure, it may be right in the eyes of God, that thou revile me him. from thence.
texts.num.23.28: So Balak took Balaam,—unto the head of Peor, that looketh over the face of the Jeshimon.
texts.num.23.29: And Balaam said unto Balak, Build me here, seven altars,—and prepare me here, seven bullocks and seven rams.
texts.num.23.30: And Balak did as Balaam said,—and caused to ascend a bullock and a ram on each altar.
texts.num.24.1: And when Balaam saw that it was good in the eyes of Yahweh to bless Israel, he went not as at other times to invoke enchantments,—but set towards the desert, his face.
texts.num.24.2: So Balaam lifted up his eyes and saw Israel, dwelling, according to his tribes,—then came upon him the Spirit of God;
texts.num.24.3: and he took up his parable, and said,—The oracle of Balaam, son of Beor, Yea the oracle of the man, of opened eye;
texts.num.24.4: The oracle of one hearing sayings of GOD, Who the sight of the Almighty, receiveth in vision, Who falleth down but hath unveiled eyes:—
texts.num.24.5: How pleasing are thy tents, O Jacob,—Thy habitations, O Israel:
texts.num.24.6: Like ravines extended, Like gardens by a river,—Like aloe-trees Yahweh hath planted, Like cedars by waters:
texts.num.24.7: He poureth forth water from his buckets, And, his seed, is among many waters,—And taller than Agag is his King, And exalted is his kingdom.
texts.num.24.8: GOD having brought him forth out of Egypt, The very horns of the buffalo, are his,—He eateth up nations that assail him And the bones of them, he breaketh And the loins of him, he crusheth:
texts.num.24.9: He hath knelt—hath lain down, Like a strong lion, yea like a lioness, Who shall rouse him up? Such as bless thee are each one blessed, But, such, as curse thee, are each one cursed.
texts.num.24.10: Then kindled the anger of Balak against Balaam, and he smote together his hands,—and Balak said unto Balaam—To revile my foes, I called thee, And lo! thou hast kept on blessing, these three times.
texts.num.24.11: Now, therefore, flee thou unto thy place,—I said, I will, highly honour, thee; but lo! Yahweh hath kept thee back from honour.
texts.num.24.12: And Balaam said unto Balak,—Was it not so that even unto thy messengers whom thou didst send unto me, I spake saying-
texts.num.24.13: Though Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, yet could I not go beyond the bidding of Yahweh, to, do good or ill, out of my own heart,—what Yahweh shall speak, that, must I speak?
texts.num.24.14: Now, therefore, behold me! going to my own people,—Come now! let me advise thee, what this people shall do unto thy people in the after-part of the days.
texts.num.24.15: So he took up his parable and said,—The oracle of Balaam, son of Beor, Yea the oracle of the man, of opened eye;
texts.num.24.16: The oracle of one hearing sayings of GOD, And knowing the knowledge of the Most High,—Who the sight of the Almighty, receiveth in vision, Who falleth down but hath unveiled eyes:—
texts.num.24.17: I see One, who is not now, I observe One, who is not nigh,—There hath marched forth a Star out of Jacob. And arisen a Sceptre out of Israel, That hath dishonoured the beard of Moab, Yea the crown of the head of all the tumultuous;
texts.num.24.18: So Edom hath become a possession, Yea a possession is Seir to his foes,—But, Israel, is doing valiantly;
texts.num.24.19: Yea One wieldeth dominion out of Jacob,—Who hath destroyed the remnant out of the fortress.
texts.num.24.20: And, when he saw Amalek, he took up, his parable, and said—The beginning of nations,—Amalek, But his latter end is even to perish.
texts.num.24.21: And when he saw the Kenite, he took up his parable, and said,—Enduring thy dwelling-place, Set thou then in the crag, thy nest;
texts.num.24.22: Yet shall it be for destruction, O Kain,—How long shall Assyria hold thee captive?
texts.num.24.23: And he took up his parable, and said,—Alas who shall survive its fulfillment by GOD;
texts.num.24.24: When, ships, [come] from the coast of the isles, And humble Assyria, and humble the Hebrew,—And he too, is even to perish?
texts.num.24.25: Then Balaam arose, and went and returned unto his place,—and, Balak also, went his way.
texts.num.25.1: And Israel remained among the acacias,—and the people began to go away unchastely unto the daughters of Moab;
texts.num.25.2: who invited the people unto the sacrifices of their gods,—so the people did eat, and did bow themselves down unto their gods.
texts.num.25.3: Thus Israel let himself be bound unto Baal-peor, and the anger of Yahweh kindled upon Israel.
texts.num.25.4: And Yahweh said unto Moses—Take all the heads of the people, and crucify them unto Yahweh. in the face of the sun,—that the heat of the anger of Yahweh may turn away from Israel.
texts.num.25.5: And Moses said unto the judges of Israel,—Slay ye each one his men, who have let themselves he bound unto Baal-peor.
texts.num.25.6: And lo! a man of the sons of Israel coming in, who brought near unto his brethren a Midianite woman, before the eyes of Moses, and before the eyes of all the assembly of the sons of Israel, when they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
texts.num.25.7: And Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest saw it, so he rose up out of the midst of the assembly, and took a spear in his hand;
texts.num.25.8: and went in after the man of Israel into the pleasure-tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel and the woman, in her parts of shame,—so the plague was restrained from against the sons of Israel.
texts.num.25.9: Then was it found that they who had died by the plague were four and twenty thousand.
texts.num.25.10: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses saying:
texts.num.25.11: Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, hath turned back my wrath from against the sons of Israel, in that he was jealous with my jealousy, in their midst, so that I made not an end of the sons of Israel. in my jealousy.
texts.num.25.12: Wherefore say,—Behold me! giving unto him my covenant of peace;
texts.num.25.13: so shall it prove to be unto him and unto his seed after him, the covenant of our age-abiding priesthood, because he was jealous for his God, and did put a propitiatory-covering over the sons of Israel.
texts.num.25.14: Now, the name of the man of Israel that was smitten, who was smitten with the Midianitish woman, was Zimri son of Salu,—prince of an ancestral house of the Simeonites;
texts.num.25.15: and, the name of the woman who was smitten, the Midianitess, was Cozbi, daughter of Zur,—the head of his kindred, of an ancestral house in Midian, was he.
texts.num.25.16: And Yahweh spake unto Moses saying:
texts.num.25.17: Besiege the Midianites,—and ye shall smite them:
texts.num.25.18: for, besiegers, were they unto you, with their wiles wherewith they beguiled you, over the matter of Peor,—and over he matter of Cozbi, daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, who was smitten in the day of the plague, over the matter of Peor.
texts.num.26.1: And it came to pass, after the plague, that Yahweh spake unto Moses, and unto Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, saying:
texts.num.26.2: Reckon ye up the sum of all the assembly of the sons of Israel from twenty years old and upwards, by their ancestral houses,—every one able to go forth to war in Israel.
texts.num.26.3: So then Moses and Eleazar the priest spake with them, in the waste plains of Moab,—by the Jordan near Jericho saying:
texts.num.26.4: From twenty years old and upwards, As Yahweh commanded Moses, and the sons of Israel, who had come forth out of the land of Egypt.
texts.num.26.5: Reuben, the firstborn of Israel,—the sons of Reuben, To Hanoch, pertained the family of the Hanochites; To Pallu, the family of the Palluites;
texts.num.26.6: To Hezron, the family of the Hezronites,—To Carmi, the family of the Carmites.
texts.num.26.7: These, are the families of the Reubenites,—and they who were numbered of them were found to be—forty-three thousand, and seven hundred, and thirty.
texts.num.26.8: Now, the sons of Pallu, were Eliab;
texts.num.26.9: and the sons of Eliab, Nemuel, and Dathan and Abiram,—The same, Dathan and Abiram, notable men of the assembly, who contended against Moses and against Aaron in the assembly of Korah, when they contended against Yahweh;
texts.num.26.10: and the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up—with Korah also, when the assembly died,—when the fire consumed two hundred and fifty men, and they became a warning;
texts.num.26.11: But, the sons of Korah, died not.
texts.num.26.12: The sons of Simeon, by their families, To Nemuel, pertained the family of the Nemuelites, To Jamin, the family of the Jaminites,—To Jachin, the family of the Jachinites:
texts.num.26.13: To Zerah, the family of the Zerahites,—To Shaul, the family of the Shaulites:
texts.num.26.14: These, are the families of the Simeonites,—two and twenty thousand and two hundred.
texts.num.26.15: The sons of Gad, by their families, To Zephon, pertained the family of the Zephonites; To Haggi, the family of the Haggites,—To Shuni, the family of the Shunites;
texts.num.26.16: To Ozni, the family of the Oznites,—To Eri, the family of the Erites;
texts.num.26.17: To Arod, the family of the Arodites,—To Arelites, the family of the Arelites:
texts.num.26.18: These, are the families of the sons of Gad, as to them who were numbered of them,—forty thousand and five hundred.
texts.num.26.19: The sons of Judah, Er and Onan,—but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
texts.num.26.20: And so, as to the sons of Judah, by their families, it was found that—To Shelah, pertained the family of the Shelanites, To Perez, the family of the Perezites,—To Zerah, the family of the Zerahites;
texts.num.26.21: And, as to the sons of Perez, it was found that—To Hezron, pertained the family of the Hezronites,—To Hamul, the family of the Hamulites:
texts.num.26.22: These, are the families of Judah, as to them who were numbered of them,—seventy-six thousand, and five hundred,
texts.num.26.23: The sons of Issachar, by their families, Unto Tola, pertained the family of the Tolaites,—To Puvah, the family of the Puvites;
texts.num.26.24: To Jashub, the family of the Jashubites,—To Shimron, the family of the Shimronites:
texts.num.26.25: These, are the families of Issachar. as to them who were numbered of them,—sixty-four thousand, and three hundred.
texts.num.26.26: The sons of Zebulun, by their families, To Sered, pertained the family of the Seredites, To Elon, the family of the Elonites,—To Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites:
texts.num.26.27: These are the families of the Zebulunites as to them who were numbered of them,—sixty thousand, and five hundred.
texts.num.26.28: The sons of Joseph by their families,—Manasseh, and Ephraim.
texts.num.26.29: The sons of Manasseh, To Machir, pertained the family of the Machirites, and, Machir, begat Gilead,—To Gilead, pertained the family of the Gileadites.
texts.num.26.30: These are the sons of Gilead: Iezer, the family of the Iezerites,—To Helek, the family of the Helekites;
texts.num.26.31: And Asriel, the family of the Asrielites; And, Shechem, the family of the Shechemites;
texts.num.26.32: And Shemida, the family of the Shemidaites; And, Hepher, the family of the Hepherites.
texts.num.26.33: Now Zelophehad, son of Hepher, had no sons, but only, daughters,—and, the names of the daughters of Zelophehad, were Mahlah and Noah, Hoglah Milcah, and Tirzah.
texts.num.26.34: These, are the families of Manasseh,—and, they who were numbered of them,—fifty-two thousand, and seven hundred.
texts.num.26.35: These are the sons of Ephraim by their families, To Shuthelah, pertained the family of the Shuthelahites, To Becher, the family of the Becherites,—To Tahan, the family of the Tahanites.
texts.num.26.36: And, these, are the sons of Shuthelah, To Eran, pertained the family of the Eranites.
texts.num.26.37: These, are the families of the sons of Ephraim, as to them who were numbered of them,—thirty-two thousand, and five hundred, These, are the sons of Joseph by their families.
texts.num.26.38: The sons of Benjamin by their families, To Bela, pertained the family of the Belaites, To Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites,—To Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites;
texts.num.26.39: To Shephupham, the family of the Shuphamites,—To Hupham, the family of the Huphamites.
texts.num.26.40: And the sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman,—[To Ard, pertained] the family of the Ardites, To Naaman, the family of the Naamites.
texts.num.26.41: These, are the sons of Benjamin by their families,—and they who were numbered of them,—were forty-five thousand and six hundred.
texts.num.26.42: These, are the sons of Dan, by their families: To Shuham, pertained the family of the Shuhamites,—These, are the families of Dan by their families:
texts.num.26.43: All the families of the Shuhamites, as to them who were numbered of them, were, sixty-four thousand, and four hundred.
texts.num.26.44: The sons of Asher, by their families: To Imnah, pertained the family of the Imnites, To Ishvi, the family of the Ishvites,—To Beriah, the family of the Beriites;
texts.num.26.45: To the sons of Beriah, To Heber, pertained the family of the Heberites, To Malchiel, the family of the Malchielites;
texts.num.26.46: And, the name of the daughter of Asher, was Serah.
texts.num.26.47: These, are the families of the sons of Asher as to them who were numbered of them,—fifty-three thousand and four hundred.
texts.num.26.48: The sons of Naphtali, by their families, To Jahzeel, pertained the family of the Jahzeelites; To Guni, the family of the Gunites:
texts.num.26.49: To Jezer, the family of the Jezerites; To Shillem, the family of the Shillemites.
texts.num.26.50: These are the families of Naphtali, by their families,—and they who were numbered of them, were forty-five thousand and four hundred.
texts.num.26.51: These, are they who were numbered of the sons of Israel, six hundred and one thousand,—seven hundred and thirty,
texts.num.26.52: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.26.53: Unto these, shall be apportioned the land as an inheritance by the number of names.
texts.num.26.54: For the large one, thou shalt make large his inheritance, and for the small one, thou shalt make small his inheritance,—unto each one, in proportion to them who were numbered of him, shall be given his inheritance.
texts.num.26.55: Nevertheless by lot, shall the land be apportioned,—by the names of the tribes of their fathers, shall they inherit.
texts.num.26.56: At the bidding of the lot, shall be apportioned his inheritance,—between large and small.
texts.num.26.57: And these, are they who were numbered of the Levites by their families, To Gershon, pertained the family of the Gershonites, To Kohath, the family of the Kohathites; To Merari, the family of the Merarites.
texts.num.26.58: These, are the families of Levi—The family of the Libnites, The family of the Hebronites, The family of the Mahlites, The family of the Mushites, The family of the Korahites,—And, Kohath, begat Amram;
texts.num.26.59: and the name of the wife of Amram, was Jochebed daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt,—and she bare to Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister:
texts.num.26.60: And, there were born to Aaron, Nadab and Abihu,—Eleazar and Ithamar;
texts.num.26.61: But Nadab and Abihu died,—when they brought near strange fire before Yahweh:
texts.num.26.62: And they who were numbered of them were found to be—twenty-three thousand, all the males from one month old and upwards—for they had not numbered themselves in the midst of the sons of Israel, because there was given unto them no inheritance, in the midst of the sons of Israel.
texts.num.26.63: These, are they who were numbered by Moses, and Eleazar, the priest,—when they numbered the sons of Israel, in the waste plains of Moab, by Jordan, near Jericho.
texts.num.26.64: And among these, was there not found a man of them who had been numbered by Moses, and Aaron the priest,—when they numbered the sons of Israel in the desert of Sinai.
texts.num.26.65: For Yahweh had said of them, They shall surely die, in the desert. And there was not left of them a man, save only, Caleb son of Jephunneh, and Joshua son of Nun.
texts.num.27.1: Then came near the daughters of Zelophehad, son of Hepher, son of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh pertaining to the families of Manasseh, son of Joseph,—these being the names of his daughters, Mahlah Noah and Hoglah and Milcah, and Tirzah.
texts.num.27.2: So they stood before Moses and before Eleazar the priest, and before the princes, and all the assembly,—at the entrance of the tent of meeting, saying:
texts.num.27.3: Our father, died in the desert, although, he, was not among the assembly that conspired against Yahweh, in the assembly of Korah,—but, in his own sin, died he; and sons, had he none.
texts.num.27.4: Wherefore should the name of our father be withdrawn out of the midst of his family, because he had no son? Give ye unto us a possession, in the midst of the brethren of our father.
texts.num.27.5: And Moses brought near their cause before Yahweh.
texts.num.27.6: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.27.7: A right thing, are the daughters of Zelophehad speaking: Thou shalt, surely give, them a possession for an inheritance, in the midst of the brethren of their father,—and shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass over unto them.
texts.num.27.8: And unto the sons of Israel, shalt thou speak, saying,—When, any man, shall die, having no son, then shall ye cause his inheritance to pass over to his daughter.
texts.num.27.9: And, if he hath no daughter, then shall ye give his inheritance unto his, brethren.
texts.num.27.10: And if he hath no brethren, then shall ye give his inheritance unto the brethren of his father.
texts.num.27.11: And, if his father hath no brethren, then shall ye give his inheritance unto his blood-relation that is near unto him of his family, and he shall possess it,—So shall it serve the sons of Israel as a regulative statute, As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.num.27.12: And Yahweh said unto Moses, Go up into this mount of Abarim,—and see, the land which I have given unto the sons of Israel;
texts.num.27.13: And, when thou hast seen it, then shalt thou also be withdrawn unto thy kinsfolk,—as Aaron thy brother was withdrawn;
texts.num.27.14: because ye resisted my bidding—in the desert of Zin when the assembly contended,—that ye should hallow me regarding the waters, before their eyes,—the same, were the waters of Meribah, of Kadesh in the desert of Zin.
texts.num.27.15: Then spake Moses unto Yahweh saying:
texts.num.27.16: Let Yahweh, God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the assembly;
texts.num.27.17: who may go out before them and who may come in before them, and who may take them out and who may bring them in,—that the assembly of Yahweh become not as sheep that have no shepherd.
texts.num.27.18: And Yahweh said unto Moses: Take thee Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is spirit,—then shalt thou lean thy hand upon him;
texts.num.27.19: and shalt cause him to stand before Eleazar the priest, and before all the assembly,—and shalt charge him before their eyes;
texts.num.27.20: and shalt put some of thine honour upon him,—that all the assembly of the sons of Israel may hearken.
texts.num.27.21: And, before Eleazar the priest, shall he stand, and shall ask by him for the decision of the Lights, before Yahweh,—at the bidding thereof, shall they go out, and at the bidding thereof, shall they come in—he, and all the sons of Israel with him, even all the assembly.
texts.num.27.22: And Moses did as Yahweh commanded him,—and took Joshua, and caused him to stand before Eleazar the priest, and before all the assembly;
texts.num.27.23: and leaned his hands upon him and charged him,—As Yahweh spake by the hand of Moses.
texts.num.28.1: And Yahweh spake unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.28.2: Command the sons of Israel, and thou shalt say unto them,—My offering, my food for my altar-flames my satisfying odour, shall ye take heed to offer unto me in its season,
texts.num.28.3: Therefore shalt thou say to them. This, is the altar-flame, which ye shall offer unto Yahweh,—he-lambs a year old, without defect, two daily, as a continual ascending-sacrifice.
texts.num.28.4: The one lamb, shalt thou offer in the morning,—and the other lamb, shalt thou offer between the two evenings;
texts.num.28.5: also the tenth of an ephah of fine meal for a meal-offering,—overflowed with beaten oil the fourth of a hin:
texts.num.28.6: a continual ascending-sacrifice,—which was offered in Mount Sinai, as a satisfying odour an altar-flame unto Yahweh.
texts.num.28.7: Also the drink-offering thereof the fourth of a hin for each lamb,—in a holy place, shall it be poured out as a libation of strong drink unto Yahweh.
texts.num.28.8: And, the other lamb, shalt thou offer between the two evenings; like the meal-offering of the morning, and like the drink-offering thereof, shalt thou offer, an altar flame a satisfying odour unto Yahweh.
texts.num.28.9: But, on the sabbath day, two he-lambs a year old without defect, and two-tenths of fine meal as a meal-offering, overflowed with oil and the drink-offering thereof:
texts.num.28.10: the ascending-sacrifice of a sabbath, on its own sabbath,—besides the continual ascending-sacrifice and the drink-offering thereof.
texts.num.28.11: And in the beginnings of your months, shall ye bring near an ascending-sacrifice unto Yahweh, two choice bullocks and one ram, seven he-lambs a year old without defect;
texts.num.28.12: and three-tenths of fine meal, as a meal-offering, overflowed with oil, to each bullock,—and two-tenths of fine-meal as a meal-offering, overflowed with oil, to each ram;
texts.num.28.13: and a tenth, severally, of fine meal as a meal-offering, overflowed with oil, to each lamb,—an ascending-sacrifice, a satisfying odour, an altar-flame unto Yahweh.
texts.num.28.14: And as their drink-offerings, half a hin, shall be to a bullock and the third of a hin to a ram, and the fourth of a hin to a lamb, of wine,—This, is the ascending-sacrifice of a month in its month, for the months of the year.
texts.num.28.15: Also one he-goat as a sin-bearer unto Yahweh,—besides the continual ascending-sacrifice, shall it be offered, with the drink-offering thereof.
texts.num.28.16: And, on the first month on the fourteenth day of the month, shall be a passover unto Yahweh;
texts.num.28.17: and, on the fifteenth day of this month, a festival,—seven days, unleavened cakes, shall be eaten.
texts.num.28.18: On the first day, a holy convocation,—no laborious work, shall ye do;
texts.num.28.19: but ye shall bring near—as an altar-flame—an ascending-sacrifice unto Yahweh,—two choice bullocks and one ram,—and seven he-lambs a year old, without defect, must they be for you;
texts.num.28.20: and, for their meal-offering, fine meal, overflowed with oil,—three-tenths for a bullock, and two-tenths for a ram, shall ye offer;
texts.num.28.21: a tenth, severally, shalt thou offer for each lamb,—for the seven lambs,;
texts.num.28.22: also one he-goat for bearing sin, to put a propitiatory-covering over you:
texts.num.28.23: in addition to the ascending-sacrifice of the morning, which is for the continual ascending-sacrifice, shall ye offer these.
texts.num.28.24: Like these, shall ye offer, daily, for seven days, as the food of the altar-flame of a satisfying odour, unto Yahweh,—besides the continual ascending-sacrifice, shall it be offered, with the drink-offering thereof.
texts.num.28.25: And on the seventh day, shall ye have, a holy convocation,—no laborious work, shall ye do.
texts.num.28.26: And on the day of firstfruits when ye bring near a new meal-offering unto Yahweh, in your weeks, a holy convocation shall there be unto you, no laborious work, shall ye do;
texts.num.28.27: but ye shall bring near as an ascending-sacrifice, for a satisfying odour unto Yahweh, two choice bullocks one ram,—seven he-lambs a year old;
texts.num.28.28: also their meal-offering, fine meal, overflowed with oil,—three-tenths for each bullock, two-tenths for the one ram;
texts.num.28.29: a tenth severally, for each lamb,—of the seven lambs;
texts.num.28.30: one young he-goat,—for putting a propitiatory-covering over you:
texts.num.28.31: in addition to, the continual ascending-sacrifice, with the meal-offering thereof, shall ye offer them,—without defect, shall they be for you, with their drink-offerings.
texts.num.29.1: And in the seventh month, on the first of the month, a holy convocation, shall there be unto you, no laborious work, shall ye do,—a day of loud acclamation, shall it be unto you.
texts.num.29.2: Therefore shall ye offer, as an ascending-sacrifice for a satisfying odour unto Yahweh, one choice bullock one ram,—seven he-lambs a year old without defect;
texts.num.29.3: and as their meal-offering, fine meal, overflowed with oil,—three-tenths to a bullock two-tenths to a ram;
texts.num.29.4: and one-tenth to each lamb,—of the seven lambs;
texts.num.29.5: and one young he-goat as a sin-bearer,—for putting a propitiatory-covering over you:
texts.num.29.6: in addition to the monthly ascending-sacrifice with the meal-offering thereof and the continual ascending sacrifice, with the meal-offering thereof and the drink-offering thereof according to their regulation,—for a satisfying odour, an altar-flame, unto Yahweh.
texts.num.29.7: And on the tenth of this seventh month, a holy convocation, shall there be unto you,—when ye shall humble your souls,—no work, shall ye do;
texts.num.29.8: but ye shall bring near, as an ascending-sacrifice unto Yahweh a satisfying odour, one choice bullock one ram,—seven he-lambs a year old, without defect, shall they be for you;
texts.num.29.9: and, as their meal-offering, fine meal overflowed with oil,—three-tenths to a bullock, two-tenths to the one ram;
texts.num.29.10: a tenth severally to each lamb,—of the seven lambs;
texts.num.29.11: one young he-goat as a sin-bearer,—in addition to, the propitiatory sin-bearer, and the continual ascending-sacrifice, with its meal-offering and their drink-offerings.
texts.num.29.12: And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, a holy convocation shall there be unto you, no laborious work, shall ye do, but ye shall celebrate a festival unto Yahweh, seven days.
texts.num.29.13: Then shall ye bring near as an ascending-sacrifice—an altar-flame of a satisfying odour unto Yahweh,—thirteen choice bullocks two rams,—fourteen he-lambs a year old without defect, shall they be;
texts.num.29.14: and, as their meal-offering, fine-meal overflowed with oil, three-tenths to each bullock of the thirteen bullocks, two-tenths to each ram, of the two rams;
texts.num.29.15: and a tenth severally, to each lamb,—of the fourteen lambs;
texts.num.29.16: also one young he-goat, as a sin-bearer,—in addition to the continual ascending-sacrifice, the meal-offering thereof and the drink-offering thereof.
texts.num.29.17: And on the second day, twelve choice bullocks two rams,—fourteen he-lambs a year old without defect;
texts.num.29.18: with their meal-offerings and their drink-offerings—to the bullocks, to the rams, and to the lambs, by their number according to the regulation;
texts.num.29.19: also one young he-goat as a sin-bearer,—in addition to the continual ascending-sacrifice, with its meal-offering, and their drink-offerings.
texts.num.29.20: And on the third day, eleven bullocks two rams,—and fourteen he-lambs a year old without defect;
texts.num.29.21: with their meal-offering and their drink-offerings, to the bullocks, to the rams, and to the lambs, by their number, according to the regulation;
texts.num.29.22: also one young he-goat as a sin-bearer, in addition to the continual ascending-sacrifice, with the meal-offering thereof and the drink-offering thereof.
texts.num.29.23: And on the fourth day, ten bullocks, two rams,—fourteen he-lambs a year old without defect;
texts.num.29.24: their meal-offering, and their drink-offerings, to the bullocks, to the rams, and to the lambs, by their number, according to the regulation;
texts.num.29.25: also one he-goat as a sin-bearer,—in addition to the continual ascending-sacrifice, the meal-offering thereof and the drink-offering thereof.
texts.num.29.26: And on the fifth day, nine bullocks two rams,—fourteen he-lambs, a year old without defect;
texts.num.29.27: with their meal-offering and their drink-offerings,—to the bullocks to the rams, and to the lambs, by their number, according to the regulation:
texts.num.29.28: also one young he-goat as a sin-bearer,—in addition to the continual ascending-sacrifice, with the meal-offering thereof and the drink-offering thereof.
texts.num.29.29: And on the sixth day, eight bullocks, two rams, fourteen he-lambs a year old without defect;
texts.num.29.30: with their meal-offering and their drink-offerings to the bullocks, to the rams, and to the lambs, by their number, according to the regulation;
texts.num.29.31: also one young he-goat as a sin-bearer,—in addition to the continual ascending-sacrifice, the meal-offering thereof and the drink-offerings thereof,
texts.num.29.32: And on the seventh day, seven bullocks, two rams, fourteen he-lambs a year old, with-out defect:
texts.num.29.33: with their meal-offering and their drink-offering, to the bullock, to the rams, and to the lambs by their number, according to their regulation;
texts.num.29.34: also one young he-goat as a sin-bearer, in addition to the continual ascending-sacrifice, the meal-offering thereof and the drink-offering thereof
texts.num.29.35: [And] on the eighth day, a closing feast shall there be unto you, no laborious work, shall ye do;
texts.num.29.36: but ye shall bring near—as an ascending-sacrifice, an altar-flame of a satisfying odour, unto Yahweh—one bullock, one ram,—seven he-lambs a year old, without defect:
texts.num.29.37: [with] their meal-offering and their drink-offerings—to the bullock to the ram, and to the lambs—by their number, according to the regulation;
texts.num.29.38: also one young he-goat as a sin-bearer,—in addition to the continual ascending-sacrifice, with the meal-offering thereof, and the drink-offering thereof.
texts.num.29.39: These, shall ye offer unto Yahweh in your appointed seasons,—besides your vow-offerings and your freewill offerings—as your ascending-sacrifices, and as your meal-offerings, and as your drink-offerings and as your peace-offerings.
texts.num.29.40: So Moses told the sons of Israel,—According to all that Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.num.30.1: And Moses spake unto the heads of the tribes of the sons of Israel saying: This, is the thing which Yahweh hath commanded-
texts.num.30.2: When, a man, shall vow a vow unto Yahweh, or swear an oath to bind a bond upon his soul, he shall not break his word,—according to all that proceedeth out of his mouth, shall he do.
texts.num.30.3: And, when, a woman, shall vow a vow unto Yahweh, and bind a bond, in the house of her father, in her youth;
texts.num.30.4: and her father shall hear her vow or her bond which she bindeth upon her soul, and her father shall hold his peace at her, then shall all her vows stand, and every bond which she hath bound upon her soul shall stand.
texts.num.30.5: But, if her father forbade her, in the day when he heard, none of her vows or her bonds which she hath bound upon her soul, shall stand,—and, Yahweh, will pardon her, because her father forbade her.
texts.num.30.6: But, if she, belonged to a husband, when her vows were taken upon her,—or a rash utterance fell from her lips, wherewith she put a bond upon her soul;
texts.num.30.7: and her husband heard it, and on the day that he heard, he held his peace at her, then shall her vows stand and her bonds which she hath bound upon her soul, shall stand,
texts.num.30.8: But if, on the day her husband heard, he forbade her, then shall he have made of none effect her vow that is upon her, or the rash utterance of her lips, wherewith she put a bond upon her soul,—and, Yahweh, will pardon her.
texts.num.30.9: But as for the vow of a widow, or of a woman divorced, whatsoever she hath bound on her soul, shall stand against her.
texts.num.30.10: But, if in the house of her husband, she vowed, or bound a bond upon her soul. with an oath;
texts.num.30.11: and her husband heard, and held his peace at her, did not forbid her, then shall all her vows stand, and every bond which she hath bound upon her soul, shall stand.
texts.num.30.12: But if her husband, did make, them, of none effect, on the day he heard, nothing which came forth out of her lips—of her vows, or of the bond of her soul, shall stand,—her husband, made it of none effect, and Yahweh, will pardon her:
texts.num.30.13: As for any vow, or any oath of binding, to humble one’s soul, her husband, may make it stand, or, her husband, may make it of none effect.
texts.num.30.14: But if her husband do hold his peace, at her, from day to day, then shall he cause all her vows to stand, or all her bonds which are upon her,—cause them to stand, because he held his peace at her, on the day when he heard.
texts.num.30.15: And, if he, do make them of none effect, after that he hath heard them, then shall he bear her iniquity.
texts.num.30.16: These are the statutes which Yahweh commanded Moses, between a man and his wife, between a father and his daughter, in her youth in the house of her father.
texts.num.31.1: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.31.2: Exact thou the avenging of the sons of Israel, from the Midianites,—and, afterwards, shalt thou be withdrawn unto thy kinsfolk.
texts.num.31.3: So Moses spake unto the people saying, Arm ye from among you men, for the war, and let them go against Midian, to render the avenging of Yahweh upon Midian.
texts.num.31.4: A thousand from each tribe,—of all the tribes of Israel, shall ye send forth unto the war.
texts.num.31.5: And there volunteered out of the thousands of Israel, a thousand of each tribe,—twelve thousand, armed for war.
texts.num.31.6: And Moses sent them a thousand of each tribe to the war,—them, and Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, to the war, with the vessels of the sanctuary, and the alarm trumpets, in his hand.
texts.num.31.7: So they made war upon Midian, as Yahweh had commanded Moses, and slew every male:
texts.num.31.8: and the kings of Midian, slew they besides their other slain namely, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, five kings of Midian,—Balaam also, son of Beor, slew they with the sword.
texts.num.31.9: And the sons of Israel took captive the women of Midian and their little ones,—all their cattle also and all their flocks and all their substance, carried they off as a prey;
texts.num.31.10: all their cities also in their sites, and all their encampments, burned they up with fire.
texts.num.31.11: Then took they all the spoil, and all the booty,—both of man and beast;
texts.num.31.12: and brought in unto Moses and unto Eleazar the priest and unto the assembly of the sons of Israel—the captives and the booty, and the spoil unto the camp,—unto the waste plains of Moab, which are by Jordan, near Jericho.
texts.num.31.13: And Moses, and Eleazar the priest and all the princes of the assembly, went forth to meet them,—unto the outside of the camp.
texts.num.31.14: Then was Moses sore displeased with the officers of the force,—the princes of thousands, and the princes of hundreds who were coming in from the warring host.
texts.num.31.15: And Moses said unto them,—Have ye saved alive every female?
texts.num.31.16: Lo! they, became unto the sons of Israel, by the advice of Balaam, the cause of daring acts of treachery against Yahweh, over the affair of Peor,—and then came the plague against the assembly of Yahweh!
texts.num.31.17: Now, therefore, slay ye every male among the young,—every woman also that hath cohabited with man, slay ye.
texts.num.31.18: But all the young of womankind that have, not cohabited with man, preserve alive for yourselves.
texts.num.31.19: Ye, then, pitch outside the camp, for seven days,—whosoever hath killed a person and whoever hath touched the slain, cleanse yourselves (from sin) on the third day and on the seventh day ye and your captives,.
texts.num.31.20: Every garment also, and every article of skin and every thing made of goat’s-hair, and every article of wood, shall ye cleanse (from sin).
texts.num.31.21: Then said Eleazar the priest unto the men of the host, who had been to the war: This, is the statute of the law, which Yahweh hath commanded Moses:
texts.num.31.22: Surely the gold and the silver,—the bronze the iron, the tin and the lead,
texts.num.31.23: whatsoever thing can go into fire, ye shall pass through fire and it shall be clean, only with the water of separation, shall ye cleanse it (from sin). But whatsoever cannot go into fire, ye shall pass through water.
texts.num.31.24: And ye shall wash your clothes on the seventh day, and be clean,—and after-wards, shall ye come into the camp.
texts.num.31.25: Then spake Yahweh unto Moses, saying:
texts.num.31.26: Reckon thou up the sum of the booty that was captured, both of man and of beast,—thou and Eleazar the priest, and the ancestral heads of the assembly;
texts.num.31.27: and divide the booty into two parts, between them who took upon them the war, who went out in the host,—and all the [rest of the] assembly.
texts.num.31.28: Then shalt thou levy a tribute unto Yahweh—from the men of war, who went forth in the host, one living thing, out of five hundred,—of the human beings, and of the herd, and of the asses and of the flock:
texts.num.31.29: out of their half, shall ye take [them],—and thou shall give [them] unto Eleazar the priest as a heave-offering unto Yahweh.
texts.num.31.30: And out of the half allotted to the sons of Israel, shalt thou take one allotted portion out of fifty of the human beings, of the herd, of the asses and of the flock of all the cattle,—and shalt give them unto the Levites, who keep the charge of the habitation of Yahweh.
texts.num.31.31: And Moses and Eleazar the priest did,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.num.31.32: And it came to pass that the booty, over and above the prey which the people of the host had seized, was,—of the flock, six hundred and seventy-five thousand;
texts.num.31.33: and, of the herd, seventy-two thousand;
texts.num.31.34: and, of the asses, sixty-one thousand;
texts.num.31.35: and, of the human persons, even of the woman-kind who had not cohabited with man,—all the persons, thirty-two thousand.
texts.num.31.36: And the half, the share of them who had gone forth in the host, was,—the number of the flock—three hundred and thirty-seven thousand and five hundred;
texts.num.31.37: and so, the tribute unto Yahweh, out of the flock, was—six hundred and seventy-five;
texts.num.31.38: and the herd, thirty-six thousand,—and the tribute of them unto Yahweh—seventy-two;
texts.num.31.39: and the asses, thirty thousand and five hundred,—and the tribute of them unto Yahweh, sixty-one;
texts.num.31.40: and the human persons, sixteen thousand,—and the tribute of them unto Yahweh, thirty-two persons.
texts.num.31.41: And Moses gave the tribute—the heave-offering of Yahweh, unto Eleazar the priest,—As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.num.31.42: And, of the half, allotted unto the sons of Israel,—which Moses halved away from the men who had gone out in the host,
texts.num.31.43: the half allotted unto the assembly, was—of the flock, three hundred and thirty-seven thousand, and five hundred;
texts.num.31.44: and, of the herd, six and thirty thousand;
texts.num.31.45: and, of asses, thirty thousand and five hundred;
texts.num.31.47: So then Moses took—out of the half belonging to the sons of Israel the allotted portion one out of fifty, of the human beings and of the beasts,—and gave them unto the Levites, the keepers of the charge of the habitation of Yahweh, As Yahweh commanded Moses.
texts.num.31.48: Then came near unto Moses the officers who belonged unto the thousands of the host,—the princes of thousands and the princes of hundreds;
texts.num.31.49: and said unto Moses, Thy servants have reckoned up the sum of the men of war who are in our hand,—and there is not missed from among us, a man!
texts.num.31.50: Therefore have we brought near an offering unto Yahweh, what, each man, hath found—articles of gold, ankle chains and bracelets, rings earrings and buckles,—to put a propitiatory-covering over our souls before Yahweh.
texts.num.31.51: So Moses, and Eleazar the priest took the gold of them,—all the wrought articles.
texts.num.31.52: And all the gold of the heave-offering which they offered up unto Yahweh, was—sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels,—of the princes of thousands, and of the princes of hundreds.
texts.num.31.53: The men of the host, had taken prey, each man for himself.
texts.num.31.54: So then Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold of the princes of thousands, and hundreds,—and brought it into the tent of meeting, as a memorial for the sons of Israel before Yahweh.
texts.num.32.1: Now, much cattle, had come into the possession of the sons of Reuben and of the sons of Gad, an exceeding mighty number. And when they saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, lo! the place, was a place for cattle.
texts.num.32.2: So the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben came in,—and spake unto Moses and unto Eleazar the priest, and unto the princes of assembly, saying,
texts.num.32.3: As touching Ataroth and Dibon, and Jazer and Nimrah, and Heshbon, and Elealeh,—and Sebam and Nebo, and Beon-
texts.num.32.4: the land which Yahweh smote before the assembly of Israel, a land for cattle, it is,—and, thy servants, have cattle.
texts.num.32.5: And they said—If we have found favour in thine eyes, let this land be given unto thy servants, for a possession,—do not take us over the Jordan.
texts.num.32.6: Then said Moses unto the sons of Gad and unto the sons of Reuben,—Shall, your brethren, go into the war, and ye, settle down here?
texts.num.32.7: Wherefore, then, should ye dissuade the heart of the sons of Israel, from passing over into the land which Yahweh hath given to them?
texts.num.32.8: Thus, did your fathers,—when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea, to view the land,
texts.num.32.9: and they went up as far as the ravine of Eschol, and viewed the land, and then dissuaded the heart of the sons of Israel from entering into the land, which Yahweh had given them.
texts.num.32.10: Then was the anger of Yahweh kindled on that day,—and he sware, saying:
texts.num.32.11: Surely none of the men that came up out of Egypt from twenty years old and upwards, shall see the soil, which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac and unto Jacob, because they have not followed after me fully;
texts.num.32.12: save Caleb son of Jephunneh, the Kenezite, and Joshua, son of Nun,—for they followed after Yahweh, fully.
texts.num.32.13: So the anger of Yahweh kindled upon Israel, and he made them wander in the desert, forty years,—until all the generation who had done the evil in the eyes of Yahweh, had wasted away!
texts.num.32.14: Lo! therefore, ye have arisen in the room of your fathers, a brood of sinful men,—to heap up yet more upon the heat of the anger of Yahweh, towards Israel.
texts.num.32.15: If ye do turn away from following him, then will he yet again leave them behind in the desert,—so shall ye bring destruction upon all this people.
texts.num.32.16: Then came they near unto him, and said, Folds, for flocks, would we build for our cattle, here,—and cities for our little ones;
texts.num.32.17: but, we, would arm ourselves promptly, before the sons of Israel, until that we have brought them into their place,—so should our little ones remain in the fortified cities, because of the inhabitants of the land.
texts.num.32.18: We would not return unto our houses,—until the sons of Israel have possessed themselves each man, of his inheritance.
texts.num.32.19: For we would not inherit with them, over the Jordan, and onwards,—because our inheritance hath come unto us on this side the Jordan towards sunrise.
texts.num.32.20: And Moses said unto them, If ye will indeed do this thing,—if ye will arm yourselves, before Yahweh, for the war;
texts.num.32.21: and every armed man of you pass over the Jordan before Yahweh,—until he hath dispossessed his enemies, from before him;
texts.num.32.22: and the land be subdued before Yahweh then afterwards, shall ye return, and shall be acquitted by Yahweh and by Israel,—and this land shall be yours for a possession before Yahweh.
texts.num.32.23: But, if ye shall not do this, lo! ye will have sinned against Yahweh,—and take note of your sin, that it will find you out.
texts.num.32.24: Build you cities for your little ones, and folds for your flocks,—and then that which hath gone forth from your mouth, ye shall do.
texts.num.32.25: Then spake the sons of Gad, and the sons of Reuben unto Moses, saying,—thy servants, will do, as, my lord, is giving command.
texts.num.32.26: Our little ones, our wives, our cattle, and all our beasts, shall remain there in the cities of Gilead;
texts.num.32.27: and thy servants, will pass over every one armed for war, before Yahweh to battle,—as, my lord is speaking.
texts.num.32.28: So Moses gave command concerning them, unto Eleazar the priest and unto Joshua son of Nun, and unto the heads of the fathers of the tribes, of the sons of Israel;
texts.num.32.29: and Moses said unto them—If the sons of Gad and the son of Reuben will pass with you over the Jordan, every one armed for the war before Yahweh, and the land be subdued before you, then shall ye give unto them the land of Gilead, for a possession.
texts.num.32.30: But, if they will not pass over armed, with you, then shall they accept a possession in your midst, in the land of Canaan.
texts.num.32.31: Then responded the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben, saying,—That which Yahweh had spoken unto thy servants, so, will we do.
texts.num.32.32: We, will pass over armed, before Yahweh into the land of Canaan,—then shall be ours, the possession of our inheritance across the Jordan.
texts.num.32.33: So then Moses gave unto them even unto the sons of Gad and unto the sons of Reuben and unto the half tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of sihon, king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og, the king of Bashan, the land by her cities with boundaries, even the cities of the land round about.
texts.num.32.34: And the sons of Gad built Dibon, and Ataroth,—and Aroer;
texts.num.32.35: and Atroth-shophan and Jazer, and Jogbehah;
texts.num.32.36: and Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran,—fortified cities and folds for flocks.
texts.num.32.37: And the sons of Reuben built Heshbon, and Elealeh,—and Kiriathaim,
texts.num.32.38: and Nebo and Baal-meon—their names being changed, and Sibmah,—and they gave names to the cities which they built.
texts.num.32.39: Then went the sons of Machir son of Manasseh to Gilead, and captured it, and dispossessed the Amorites who were therein,
texts.num.32.40: So Moses gave Gilead unto Machir son of Manasseh, and he dwelt therein.
texts.num.32.41: And Jair, son of Manasseh, went, and captured their encampments,—and called them Havvoth-jair [="The encampments of Jair"].
texts.num.32.42: And, Nobah, went, and captured Kenath, with the villages thereof,—and called it Nobah, after his own name.
texts.num.33.1: These, are the departures of the sons of Israel whereby they came forth out of the land of Egypt by their hosts,—in the hand of Moses and Aaron.
texts.num.33.2: And Moses wrote their comings forth by their departures, at the bidding of Yahweh,—and these, are their departures by their comings forth.
texts.num.33.3: So then they brake up from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month, on the morrow of the passover, came forth the sons of Israel with an uplifted hand, in the sight of all the Egyptians;
texts.num.33.4: when the Egyptians, were burying them whom Yahweh had smitten among them, every firstborn,—when, upon their gods, Yahweh had executed judgments,
